about: The one coverage inventory (plan section 7): every ACT feature with its stable id, source, contracts and verification; the reviewed index of every surface static and live discovery finds; a review stamp for every application source file; and the issue ledger behind every planned gap. The feature-map documents in files/dev-work/feature-map/ describe the features in prose and name only their ids; the mapping lives here alone. Routine kinds (behavior, native, media, control, discovery) are what the routine gate runs and must satisfy; release kinds (qualification, owner, planned) stay pending and keep release_ready false. helpers/inventory.py checks this file; restamp a source file only after reviewing its features.

method: static AST discovery of controls, dialogs, bindings and tools over the application registry
live widget trees of an isolated real instance: the shell, six tools, Preferences and four speech-engine states
source and test reading per tool; every test id resolved against the collected suite at 118058c or by AST
registered journeys mapped by the layers they really give
limits: Windows only, at 100% display scaling (96 DPI)
optional engines in their isolated, not-installed state
dialog contents are indexed by their call sites, not opened live

features.title: Import PDF and TXT sources into the one queue
contracts: Only PDF and TXT can be queued: the catalog offers exactly .pdf and .txt and both are selected by default; EPUB is retired.
Add Files keeps the order the dialog returned; Add Folder recurses into subfolders by default, skips hidden folders unless allowed and refuses a file already queued unless duplicates are allowed.
A drive or home-folder root is confirmed before any scan thread starts, and a large result is confirmed before anything is committed; declining leaves the queue as it was.
Move Up, Move Down, Remove and Clear All change only the queue, never a file on disk.
Cancel Import stops the scan only; it never reaches a conversion run, and a conversion Cancel never reaches the scan.

features.title: Start a conversion run (validate, freeze, reserve, settle)
contracts: Start with an empty queue warns 'Missing input' and reserves nothing.

On Start everything the run uses (queue, backend and voice id, voice label, bitrate, workers, rate, resume, overwrite, the voice's pauses, speech preparation) is frozen once; later changes to widgets, the queue or files on disk cannot reach the run.
The numbered run folder is reserved only after validation; a reservation or naming refusal shows 'Output folder' and leaves no empty folder.
One file that fails is a retryable item failure and the run goes on; a run that itself breaks is a non-retryable job failure, and the panel always returns to idle.
A run ends once, as Succeeded, Completed with failures, Cancelled or Failed.
An Edge rate the Edge voices would refuse, for a queue with folder-imported files, is refused at Start ('Edge speech rate') before anything is frozen or reserved (ACT.TTS.EDGE-RATE).

features.title: Narrate a directly added file with the Edge chapter engine
contracts: A directly added PDF or TXT with an Edge voice takes the chapter engine and lands flat in the run folder as <stem>-<voice label>.mp3 at the chosen bitrate.

In a TXT, 'Title:'/'Author:' lines are metadata, '#' lines start chapters, a heading is spoken only when it holds speakable text, two headings in a row are joined and spoken as one title, and a UTF-8 BOM is ignored.

The voice's frozen preset sets the sentence, paragraph, title and chapter pauses; commas, ellipses and dashes get short pauses inside a sentence; Edge padding is trimmed from sentence clips; nothing follows the last word.
Every sentence is sent to the service once, in order, with nothing omitted or duplicated; the Edge speech rate box is not applied to direct files.

all_of.detail: Listen to a real direct Edge narration: chapter titles spoken where the author wrote them, natural sentence, paragraph, title and chapter pauses, comma/dash/ellipsis pauses, nothing skipped or repeated.

features.title: Narrate folder-imported files with the Edge chunked route
contracts: A file found under an imported folder is narrated in chunks of about 3000 characters at the frozen Edge rate, with 0.8 s between requests and 50 ms between joined chunks.
Its output mirrors its folder's relative path inside the run folder; several imported roots each get their own collision-safe container.
On this route 'Title:' and '#' lines are spoken as written; a UTF-8 BOM is ignored; no text is lost or duplicated by chunking.
The chunks are joined into one MP3 at the chosen bitrate, checked, and published whole.

all_of.detail: Listen to a real folder-route narration at a non-default rate: pace follows the rate, chunk joins are not audible, nothing skipped or repeated.

features.title: Edge online speech requests, retries and failure advice
contracts: Only a failure another attempt can cure (network or temporary service trouble, or one not understood) is retried; a refused handshake (HTTP 401/403), a changed protocol or a local file problem is not.
Direct route: at most 3 attempts per clip with doubling, jittered waits (1-3 s, then 2-6 s). Folder route: at most 5 attempts per chunk (2, 4, 8, 16 s) and 2 more whole-file attempts.
A final service failure gives the item one line of plain advice in its failure message, while the scrubbed technical detail (no handshake tokens, no book text) goes to Details.
A failed attempt leaves no partial clip; edge-tts is pinned at 7.3.1 and an install that drifted from the pin is named in the advice.

features.title: Cancel a running conversion
contracts: Cancel only requests a stop; the run shows Cancelled after a worker acknowledges it at a checkpoint and has cleaned up, never because the button was pressed.
Cancel wakes the FFmpeg watchdog and the memory gate at once, wakes a paused run and outranks the pause.
Files published before the Cancel stay; nothing unfinished is saved; a file that had started is logged as stopped and one that never started as skipped, and Retry Failed offers neither.
The run's closing line counts the files finished, stopped (nothing unfinished saved) and not started; each file's own line already tells stopped from skipped (v0.7.2, ACT72-004).

features.title: Cancel and the final rename are ordered
contracts: Each attempt at the rename that makes a file final first asks for authorization on the same lock the Cancel latch is taken under; whichever comes first wins and both sides know.
A Cancel that wins publishes nothing, leaves the destination untouched and removes the staging file; a Cancel during the copy into staging publishes nothing.
A commit that wins finishes whole and stays; the Cancel is told a commit may still land and the run is not reported cancelled until it has.
The lock is never held across the flush or the rename, so Cancel never waits for the disk.

features.title: Cancel ends an Edge request and its waits
contracts: A request in flight on either Edge route is abandoned within a bounded time after Cancel and its partial clip is removed.
No further request and no remaining back-off or inter-chunk wait happens after Cancel.
A request that refuses to stop is dropped within the bound, stops running, and the log says so.
With eight files requesting at once, none makes a request after the latch.

features.title: Cancel ends a wait at the memory gate
contracts: A file waiting at the memory gate stops waiting as soon as Cancel is latched, whether or not its synthesis is complete, and assembles nothing.
The panel's Cancel wakes the gate so the wait ends before the next poll.
A Cancel during an in-memory assembly starts no fall-back to disk, and the wait before a second disk attempt also ends on Cancel.

features.title: Cancel kills the run's FFmpeg within one look
contracts: Every FFmpeg a TTS conversion starts through pydub runs under the conversion's cancel check and is killed within one 0.25 s look once Cancel is latched, however well it is progressing.
The panel's Cancel wakes the watchdog so the kill does not wait for its next look.
Kokoro and Chatterbox encodes run under the same control; nothing unfinished reaches a destination.

features.title: Cancel clicked for real with requests in flight
contracts: A real click on Cancel while Edge requests are in flight stops the run inside its time budget.
No further request is made after the click and nothing is published.

features.title: Pause and resume between source files
contracts: Pause is a request: files already converting finish, the run shows Paused once the workers acknowledge it, and no new source file starts while paused.
Pause is honoured only between source files, never inside a chapter, chunk, request or PDF extraction.
Resume continues the queue to the end; a pause requested as the run ends never leaves a paused final state.

features.title: Pause and Resume clicked for real at a file boundary
contracts: With one worker and two files, a real Pause lets the active file finish and starts nothing new.
A real Resume completes the queue and both outputs are real MP3s.

features.title: Retry Failed re-runs only the failed files of the frozen run
contracts: Retry Failed is offered only when the settled run has a retryable failure, and re-runs exactly those occurrences with the run's original frozen snapshot (voice, label, bitrate, rate, overwrite, speech preparation).
A retried file lands on the destination its original run planned; no new run folder is reserved and nothing is re-planned.
A retry never overwrites an earlier success and never skips a file because of its own failed remains.
Changing widgets, the queue or the configuration after the run cannot change what the retry does.

features.title: A source with nothing to read fails cleanly
contracts: A PDF with no extractable text fails its item with a named reason ('No readable text found in PDF. File may be scanned/image-based.'), makes no request and publishes nothing.
An empty, header-only, heading-only or punctuation-only TXT fails on the direct route before any request; a BOM-only TXT is no text on the folder route.
A narration that comes out silent is refused, never published as a success; the source file is never changed.

features.title: Extract and clean PDF text
contracts: PDF text comes from PyMuPDF with a page number printed as the first or last line of a page removed before lines are joined, words hyphenated across lines and across pages joined, soft-wrapped lines rejoined, the remaining digit-only and short all-caps lines removed and paragraphs merged across page breaks.
Only one PyMuPDF call runs at a time in the process, so files converting side by side each get their own text.
A directly added PDF with no '#' heading gets its first text line as the spoken chapter title (never the file name), removed once from the body.
Every route that reads a PDF (Edge direct, Edge folder, Kokoro, Chatterbox, Qwen3) uses this one extractor.

Known limits of the cleaning (ACT72-064): a running head longer than four capitals is narrated as a heading; a line that is only a one-to-four-letter all-caps word is dropped wherever it is; a compound word broken at its own hyphen loses the hyphen; a bare number that is a page's last line is taken for its page number.

features.title: A narration ends with its last sound
contracts: Only the terminal near-silent suffix is shortened, to at most about 300 ms after the last sound at -60 dBFS (at least 150 ms kept, and never before the last sound at -70 dBFS); leading and internal silence are never touched.
Quiet sound past the budget is kept in full and the log asks for listening; a recording that stops while still sounding is flagged, never cut.
No route adds a closing pause; the end-of-book pause is accepted for compatibility and adds nothing.

all_of.detail: Listen to the last seconds of real narrations on each route, especially any the Details log marks 'please listen to the ending'.

features.title: Publish each MP3 whole, and Overwrite only when asked
contracts: The final name appears only once the MP3 is finished, checked, staged beside the destination, flushed and renamed in one same-filesystem operation; a failed or cancelled attempt leaves nothing under the final name and removes only its own staging file.
With Overwrite off (the default) an existing file is never replaced, including one that appears during synthesis; a doomed file is refused before any synthesis.
With Overwrite ticked for that run the old file stays valid until the new one takes its name; a link or folder is never replaced.
An empty, silent, over-24-hour, non-MP3, truncated or wrong-length result is refused.

features.title: Skip MP3s already in this run
contracts: With Resume ticked (the default), a folder-route item whose planned output already exists is skipped on a first attempt and logged 'Skipping (already exists)'.
Resume never applies to directly added files or to Retry Failed.

The box says only what it does, "Skip MP3s already in this run": a new run starts in a newly reserved folder and never continues an earlier one, so in the app it has nothing to skip; it was labelled "Resume (skip existing MP3s)" until v0.7.2 (ACT72-046). The command line's --resume is unchanged.

features.title: Output names <stem>-<voice label>.mp3 and collision-safe planning
contracts: Every route names its file <source stem>-<voice label frozen at Start>.mp3; the engine adds no suffix and a later voice rename cannot move a run or its retry.
Stem and label are cleaned separately (forbidden characters and separators become '_', NFC normalised) and a Windows device name before the first dot is guarded.
When a path would be too long only the stem is shortened, from its end; a label or folder that cannot fit is refused at Start before any synthesis.
Clashes (same stem, PDF and TXT, case or Unicode spelling, deliberate duplicates, existing files) get the shared planner's -1, -2 numbering; no planned destination is ever an input.

features.title: Numbered run folder and Open Output Folder
contracts: Opening the panel, importing or switching tools creates no folder; the read-only Output field shows where the next run will go and follows a change made in Preferences & Data.
A validated Start reserves exactly one numbered run folder (TTS-Audiobook-N) for the whole mixed queue, and the Output field then shows it.
Open Output Folder reveals this run's folder, or the tool's parent folder before any run; a folder that cannot be made is reported, not raised.

features.title: File workers: requested versus effective concurrency
contracts: The Workers box accepts 1 to 100 whole-file workers; one worker owns one file and a file's own chapters and chunks stay in order.

The run uses min(requested, queued files, engine ceiling, Edge service ceiling of 32, logical processors, what memory fits) and the Details log always states 'Requested workers: N | Effective workers: M' and, when lower, which limit applied.
Kokoro, Chatterbox and Qwen3 always convert one file at a time; only Edge runs files side by side.
Direct and folder Edge files share one pool and each converts in its own private working folder.

features.title: Memory-safe assembly and supervised FFmpeg
contracts: While synthesising, a file holds at most about 16 MB of audio in memory; a longer paragraph or clip is written out losslessly as it grows.

Before a whole narration is assembled the gate checks its real size against free memory and commit: in memory if it fits, wait if other files are holding memory, otherwise on disk, which gives the same MP3 to the byte.

If memory runs out after the gate said yes, the same audio is assembled on disk once more without asking the service again; if even that cannot run, the file fails with a reason that names memory and suggests Retry Failed.
Every FFmpeg on these routes is supervised: it cannot deadlock on its pipes, and one making no progress for 300 s is killed and the file fails with a reason.

features.title: MP3 bitrate choice
contracts: The MP3 bitrate dropdown offers 128k, 192k (default) and 320k and is frozen per run.
The frozen bitrate reaches every route: Edge direct, Edge folder and the three local engines.
Each offered bitrate produces an internally consistent MP3 whose header and frames agree.

Every voice makes 24 kHz speech, where an MP3 can be at most 160 kbit/s: 192k and 320k are written at 160k, and the run's Summary says so at Start. The request itself is frozen unchanged and nothing is resampled (v0.7.2, ACT72-021; measured on the app's real output of every engine).

features.title: Edge speech rate for folder-imported files
contracts: The Edge speech rate field is shown only for an Edge voice and takes its default from the voice preset (+0%).
The typed rate is frozen per run and sent with every folder-route Edge request; directly added Edge files always use Edge's natural pace.
Worker planning reads the rate as a speed for the folder route and ignores it for the direct route.

Start refuses a rate the Edge voices would refuse (anything but a sign, a whole number and %), before anything is frozen or reserved, whenever folder-imported files would send it; a queue of directly added files never judges it.

features.title: Choose a voice; registered is not the same as available
contracts: The dropdown lists the 28 registered voices in registry order and starts on Edge Male - Steffan; no voice choice is saved.
A voice's identity is (backend, voice id); its label only names files and selects nothing; an invalid registry (duplicate, empty or padded labels, unknown backend, missing default) refuses to load.
Selecting a voice shows its engine line, its rate or speed control (or none), its notices, and a status line when it cannot run on this computer.

Availability is asked again at Start: a label that names no registered voice is refused ('Voice not recognised') and a voice that cannot run and cannot be installed is refused ('Voice unavailable'); no other voice or engine is substituted.

features.title: Ask before downloading the English sentence data
contracts: Only an Edge run with a directly added file needs the sentence data; folder-only Edge runs and local engines never ask.
When it is missing or damaged, Start asks first, naming the size, the source and the folder; nothing is downloaded silently.
No, a failed download or Cancel starts nothing, reserves no folder and says so; Yes downloads it in a small modal window off the Tk thread and then starts that same run.
The worker only proves the data is present and never downloads; if it vanished meanwhile the run fails with a message saying what to do.
Every message that asks the person to try again names the button they see: Start.

features.title: Install a missing voice and continue the same run
contracts: When the chosen voice is only missing installable files, Start freezes the run first and opens the review-and-install window; nothing is reserved before the voice is installed.
After a successful install the voice is checked again and the same frozen run starts exactly once; later changes to the panel are not read.
Skip, Cancel, a failure, closing the window or closing the panel abandons the run and creates nothing; a source changed or removed during the install stops the run with a message.
A second Start while the install window is open opens nothing and starts nothing.
Every message that asks the person to try again names the button they see: Start.

features.title: Speech preparation of numbers, dates, symbols and glossary words
contracts: The setting (tts.speech_prep, default v1) is read once at Start: the bundled mode table, optional user mode overrides and the bundled and user glossaries are validated and frozen by value; edits during a run or before Retry Failed never reach it.

With v1, each route rewrites only the classes its engine's cells set to 'expand' (from the owner's G1 verdicts), applies glossary entries with the user's first, and never changes protected spans or 'Title:'/'Author:'/'#' markers.
Every rewrite is proved to rebuild the source exactly; if a proof fails that file is spoken unchanged and Details says so; a broken user file contributes nothing and one note, never a failed run.
With 'off' the text reaches every engine exactly as decoded and Details says nothing.

all_of.detail: Listen to numbers, years, dates, times, currency, units and any glossary words as each engine speaks them with speech preparation on.

features.title: Activity log, progress and estimate
contracts: Summary shows the run's state, progress, failures and ending; Detailed also carries each step and the engines' own output, which never reaches Summary.
Engine output is queued as whole lines, each prefixed with its file name while several files convert; partial lines are flushed when a file or the run ends.
Events reach the log in the order they were numbered; one progress bar counts finished source files, and the estimate learns only from this attempt's own timings.
Clear Log empties both visible panes only; the run's result and Retry Failed are untouched. Each run or retry adds a divider so earlier history stays.

features.title: Responsive layout and appearance of the TTS panel
contracts: Wide windows put the workflow (Sources over Voice & Audio over Output & Run) left and Activity right; 920x600 and 1024x720 use the split arrangement with Activity still on the right; only a smaller panel stacks Activity beneath.
Every required control stays wholly on screen at 920x600, 1024x720 and larger; only the queue list and the log scroll, each with a measured floor; no whole-panel scrollbar.
A voice notice appearing or disappearing re-measures the layout; switching Light/Dark recolours everything without moving any state or a running job.
Every Kokoro, Chatterbox and Qwen3 voice state, installed or not, keeps Start and Cancel on screen at 920x600 and larger.

A Qwen3 voice's hardware and speed disclosure is shown in full wherever it fits (1024x720 and larger); only where the split arrangement cannot fit it (the 920x600 minimum) is it presented as a 'Hardware and speed...' button beside Install / repair, reachable by Tab, that shows the complete text. The minimum size, the queue and log floors and every action stay as they are.

all_of.detail: Approve the captured TTS panel candidates at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900.
Check the TTS panel at Windows display scaling above 100% (for example 125% and 150%).

features.title: Controls lock while a run is active
contracts: While a run is active Start, File workers, Overwrite, Resume, the Edge speech rate, the Kokoro speed, Install / repair Qwen3 voices, the bitrate and voice dropdowns and the queue editing are locked through the shared lock matrix, and unlock when it ends with every value as it was (v0.7.2, ACT72-014).
Open Output Folder, Clear Log and Cancel Import are never locked by a run.

features.title: Working files are removed, and an interrupted run's leftovers are swept
contracts: Each conversion's temporary folders and files are entries of one process's workspace in the TTS work area (%TEMP%\act-tts\<16-hex token>\<n>): the Edge engine's folder, the panel's direct and local-engine folders, pydub's temporaries and the local engines' encode WAV. Nothing of a conversion lies loose in the temp folder. The folder route's chunks stay in .tmp_chunks/<pid>-<token> beside the run.

A workspace's manifest names its owner by process id and process creation time and lists every entry (kind, retention, state) before the entry's folder exists; it is replaced in one operation after its bytes reach the disk.

An entry is removed when its conversion ends, however it ends (finished, cancelled or failed), and a failed pydub export's temporaries with it. One another program still holds is left 'finished' and removed at a later start; the last entry to go takes the manifest and the workspace with it.

At the start of each run (the panel and the command line), only a workspace whose manifest is intact and whose owner is provably gone (no such process, its id reused by another process, or exited) loses its disposable entries, then its manifest and itself. A running or unverifiable owner, a missing, partial, damaged or foreign manifest, a name this tool does not make, a link, an entry not marked disposable and a file in use are left exactly as they are, and each except a running owner is named in Detailed. Nothing outside the work area is examined. Recovery stops at 5 s or at Cancel and finishes at a later start.

Removal never follows a link: the temp folder and every folder down to the one being emptied are held open without delete sharing, so none can be renamed or replaced meanwhile; every entry is opened without following a reparse point, judged by that handle and deleted through it. A link is left and reported; a hard link loses only the work area's name.

At the start of each run, staging files and chunk folders left under the output tree by a process that is gone and untouched for an hour are removed; anything named otherwise, any link and a live run's work are left alone.

features.title: Closing the panel or window during work
contracts: Closing retires the run's reporting first, asks the run to cancel (which also wakes a paused run), waits up to 5 s for the worker, then closes the importer, the job adapter and the pump; nothing stays scheduled.
Closing is idempotent and quiet with a report in flight.
Alt+F4 during narration exits with status 0, no window, no owned process and no Tcl crash.
A forced collection on a worker after close makes no Tk call and takes well under a second (about 23 s for TTS and 17 s for Cover before v0.7.2 Phase 6, ACT72-017).

features.title: Standalone command-line converters (developer only)
contracts: batch_convert --input <folder> converts every PDF/TXT below it to <stem>-<label>.mp3, mirroring subfolders, never overwriting an earlier output (it is numbered instead) unless --resume skips it.
An unregistered --speaker needs --label and nothing is synthesised without one; workers are held to the same limits as the app.
epub2tts-edge <file> publishes through the same contract as the app and can also make an M4B with chapters and a cover; a failed FFmpeg step raises (exit status 1).

Ctrl+C during either FFmpeg step of --format m4b (the concat into FLAC-in-MP4, the AAC encode with the chapters) stops that step's own FFmpeg within a fraction of a second, through its own process handle (terminate, then kill after a 2 s grace; any other FFmpeg, even one this process started, is untouched), starts no further step and publishes nothing; a Ctrl+C between or after the steps publishes nothing either; further presses while the step is being stopped cannot cut the stopping short; the command line prints one line and exits 130

Each of those two steps has a deadline: the book's playing time, read from its parts' headers, plus ten minutes. A step still running then is stopped and reaped the same way, nothing is published and the command line exits 124; a longer book's steps get a longer deadline, so a working step is never cut short

However a run ends early (Ctrl+C, the deadline, a failed step), what the output folder already held, a file under the run's own name with --overwrite included, and the sources are unchanged, and the run's work folder (the .m4a and any half-written .m4b) is removed

features.title: Local-engine files in the shared run
contracts: A Kokoro, Chatterbox or Qwen3 run is the same run: same queue, controller, progress, planner and publication; only the synthesis call differs, chosen by the frozen backend.
A PDF goes through the one PDF extractor first; a TXT is handed over as it stands.
A destination that could not be published is refused before the model is loaded; the engine writes to a private scratch path and the MP3 reaches its destination through the publication contract.
One file at a time; Cancel reaches the engine through the run's cancel check (Kokoro and Chatterbox encodes also under the FFmpeg watch).

features.title: Kokoro local narration
contracts: One source file becomes one MP3: chunks of at most 3000 characters, split at sentence ends, are rendered in order and encoded exactly once at the model's 24 kHz rate.
The chunk pause (default 50 ms) separates rendered chunks only; no closing pause is added whatever end_silence_ms says.
Cancel is honoured between chunks and again just before the single encode; a cancelled file writes nothing.
The first pipeline load in a process is retried once after 2 s (Windows Application Control); any later load failure is reported with a repair hint, never retried.

The Kokoro speed from the panel is passed to the model unchanged once Start has accepted it: a finite number from 0.5 to 2.0; anything else is refused before anything is frozen or reserved (v0.7.2, ACT72-047).

all_of.detail: Listen to real Kokoro narration from an installed copy: pacing, pronunciation, no clipped ending.

features.title: Chatterbox Turbo cloned-voice narration
contracts: Text is split by Chatterbox's own splitter into pieces under its ceiling; a plan that loses, duplicates or reorders any non-whitespace character is refused.
A generated chunk with an internal near-silent run is re-drawn a bounded number of times, then the file fails rather than publish a defective draw.
Cancel is checked between chunks; a cancelled file leaves no output.
The chunk pause separates chunks only; no closing pause is added.
The device is chosen at runtime: CUDA, then MPS, then CPU.

all_of.detail: Listen to real Chatterbox Turbo narration in each of the six cloned voices.

features.title: Qwen3-TTS preset and cloned-voice narration
contracts: Each source file is narrated by one worker subprocess in the separate Qwen3 engine environment; the GUI process never imports the model stack.
Chunks are whole sentences that never cross a paragraph, preserve every source character in order, and carry a stable per-chunk seed.

Chunk audio is read back from the files in plan order, validated (mono, finite, same rate), assembled with pauses between chunks only, encoded once and published atomically; cancel wins until the moment of the move.
A reported failure (load, generation, out of memory) fails that file with a plain message, leaves any existing destination untouched and removes the job folder.
Windows only; on other platforms the voices say 'not yet available' and nothing is offered.

all_of.detail: Listen to real Qwen3 narration in the two preset and six cloned voices (calm clone profile).

features.title: Qwen3 worker supervision, cancel and containment
contracts: The worker is started suspended inside a kill-on-close Windows Job Object; if it cannot be contained it is never run and the user is told why.
Cancel sets a flag the worker checks before loading and before every chunk; a worker that ignores it is killed after a grace period, together with every child process.
A worker that stalls, exits without exactly one terminal event, or reports success and then crashes or hangs is a failed file with its own error text.
Only protocol events count as progress, so flooding output cannot postpone a cancel or the stall watchdog.

features.title: Qwen3 one-operation-at-a-time locks
contracts: A conversion holds the inference lease (this copy's inference.lock plus a machine-wide Global\ mutex) for its whole run; an install or repair cannot start meanwhile, and a conversion cannot start during an install or repair.
Across every copy of the app on the computer only one heavy Qwen3 model operation runs at a time; the machine guard never waits and fails closed (busy or denied refuse with a message).
A running worker holds engine.lock, so a repair of the app's environment refuses while the engine is in use.
The operating system releases every lock when its holder dies, so a crash never leaves a stale lock.

features.title: Local engines convert one file at a time
contracts: Whatever the Workers box asks (up to 100), a Kokoro, Chatterbox or Qwen3 run converts exactly one file at a time on any machine.
The run log says why: 'Worker limit: <engine> converts one file at a time.'
No concurrency expansion: the per-process Kokoro pipeline and Chatterbox model caches are not reentrant and are never shared by two files at once.

features.title: Local engines never download at narration time
contracts: Kokoro and Chatterbox load only the pinned, verified local files; a missing, wrong-size or wrong-hash file is refused with AssetsUnavailable ('Nothing was downloaded') instead of letting the library fetch it.
A Kokoro voice with no pinned file is refused, not fetched; a missing spaCy English model is refused before misaki could pip-install it.
Chatterbox loads from the pinned commit's folder (from_local), never from_pretrained at a moving branch.
The Qwen3 worker runs with the Hugging Face hub and transformers offline and every cache inside the app folder.

features.title: Installed or missing: local voice availability
contracts: Each local voice answers (ok, reason) cheaply and deterministically from files on disk: no model load, no download, no write, never an exception.
Qwen3 checks in a fixed order (platform, engine, model, then reference and transcript for clones) and each reason names one next step.

A voice whose models are simply not installed maps to its optional component and is offered Install & Continue; anything installing cannot fix (missing reference, unsupported platform, busy engine) is not offered.
One unavailable voice never makes another voice or engine unavailable, and is never swapped for another voice.
Tests state the machine's install state explicitly (installed, or a fresh install), never the machine they run on; simulated readiness is asset health only, never engine qualification.

features.title: Cloned voices' reference recordings and transcripts
contracts: A clone is used only when its bundled reference recording matches its registered SHA-256; a missing or changed recording blocks only that voice and is never replaced by download or by another voice.

Qwen3 clones narrate with the six owner-approved transcripts shipped with the app; a damaged or missing bundle blocks the clones with 'extract a fresh copy' guidance and never falls back to a local store.
The protected recordings are never written; derived clips and cached conditionals live only under files/runtime-data and are recomputed when their source, engine or spec changes.
A Qwen3 clone job clones a verified copy of the recording (padded with silence) made inside the job folder, not the original path.

features.title: Install the Kokoro voices
contracts: Installing Kokoro acquires exactly the pinned model, one .pt per roster voice and the approved spaCy English wheel, at the pinned commit, never a moving main.
The spaCy wheel is size- and hash-checked before pip sees it, installed offline with --no-index --no-deps --require-hashes, and kept so a rebuilt environment can reinstall it without downloading.
Success is claimed only after the files are hashed again, recorded and the Kokoro engine is proved to load.
From the TTS panel, Install & Continue starts the frozen run exactly once after a successful install; Skip, Cancel or a failure starts nothing and creates nothing.

The panel shows one Kokoro message at a time: while the voice can run, that it runs locally from its installed model files (no download is promised); while it cannot, the setup line naming Install & Continue.

features.title: Install the Chatterbox Turbo model
contracts: Installing Chatterbox acquires exactly the Turbo files the engine loads (not s3gen.safetensors), at the pinned commit.
The download can never exceed what was confirmed: a file lost or changed after the plan was shown fails the install and asks for a new plan.
Success is claimed only after the files are verified and the Chatterbox package is proved to import.
Missing reference recordings are not installable; they block only their own voice.

features.title: Install Qwen3 voices (CustomVoice, Base or both)
contracts: Nothing downloads until a button is pressed and the confirmation, which states the engine, each model, shared files, total download and disk space, is answered Yes.
CustomVoice (two presets) and Base (six clones) install independently; 'Install Both' fetches the files they share once; installed parts are not offered again.
Every file is accepted only when its size and SHA-256 match the manifest; an interrupted download resumes from its .part with a Range request.
Cancel keeps what completed and the next install fetches only the rest; a model is never reported installed half-way; too little disk space is refused before anything is downloaded.
While an install runs the other actions and Close are disabled; closing the window cancels the work first and closes once it has stopped.

features.title: Check and repair the Qwen3 voices
contracts: Check and repair first runs a read-only full check (engine start-up probe and the SHA-256 of every installed file) and changes nothing.
What is wrong and what fixing it would download is shown and acted on only after Yes; No changes nothing; a clean check says so and asks nothing.
Repair re-fetches only the files that fail and rebuilds an engine that will not start, removing only the app's own canonical engine folder.
A folder that cannot be shown to be the app's own environment is never deleted.

features.title: Qwen3 engine environment
contracts: The engine is created at .venv/engines/qwen3 directly from the verified base CPython 3.12, never from the app's own interpreter; an older .venv-qwen3 is used while it is the only engine and is never installed into, rebuilt or deleted.
Every package is the reviewed manifest's exact wheel (89), fetched and hash-verified once, then installed offline with --no-index --require-hashes --only-binary; pip never reaches an index.
The install is recorded only after the worker's probe imports the whole stack; a failed pip or probe is an incomplete install, with downloaded wheels kept for the retry.
The engine is ready only with its interpreter, a live base Python, a recorded probe and matching requirements; otherwise the status says to rebuild.

features.title: Developer tools: Qwen3 reference transcripts
contracts: In normal mode (the shipped developer_mode = false) the button is never created, the dialog cannot be built and every step refuses when called directly.
The speech recognizer is downloaded only after a confirmation that states its size; drafts are made locally from verified copies of the recordings and saved unapproved.
Approval needs the 'I listened' tick and non-empty text and is bound to the recording's SHA-256; a draft is never an approval.
Narration keeps using the shipped bundle unless the developer confirms a per-voice selection; 'Use the shipped texts' removes it.

features.title: Optional voice setup plan and disclosure
contracts: For each of the four components (Kokoro, Chatterbox Turbo, Qwen3 CustomVoice, Qwen3 Base) the plan states one readiness: ready, missing, damaged, unsupported, busy, bad bundle or unverified; only missing (install) and damaged (repair) plan any acquisition.

It lists what would be downloaded, reused, copied, occupied and needed as temporary space, counting shared Qwen3 files once, and says how each figure is known (manifest, approximate, at least, unknown).
Planning is read-only: it writes nothing into the installation and starts no process (except an optional bounded nvidia-smi query).
The pre-venv estimate used by the first-run wizard is a manifest upper bound that proves nothing (every component unverified).

features.title: Consent-bound acquisition (no silent downloads)
contracts: A consent is bound to the fingerprint of the exact plan shown; a forged, unrelated, stale, altered or inflated consent acquires nothing.
A consent is spent once and never replayed; a retry needs a fresh plan and a fresh confirmation.
All network access goes through an opener that refuses any URL outside the confirmed files and charges a byte budget fixed by the consent.
Every write is proved, at the moment of writing, to lie inside its own folder with no link on the way.

features.title: Setup worker operation and its single outcome
contracts: Every request ends in exactly one terminal outcome (succeeded, refused, cancelled or failed), published once and never replaced.
Cancel is honoured at every checkpoint and during transfers, pip and the health proof, giving one cancelled result; a partial file is kept for a later consented resume.
An install succeeds only when every chosen component is proved working afterwards; otherwise it fails naming what was proved.
A failure in one component leaves healthy voices and their files exactly as they were.
The worker runs only in the app's own CPython 3.12 environment and acquires nothing for a plan request.

features.title: Local engine health probes and busy detection
contracts: Kokoro and Chatterbox health is proved in a fresh interpreter with the Hugging Face hub offline, bounded in time and cancellable; the answer is tri-state (proved, proved broken, unproved), and a probe that cannot finish is never 'broken'.
A probe is repeated only while Windows Application Control is still evaluating new files, a bounded number of times; any other failure is reported at once.
A component someone else is changing or using (a held lock) is reported busy and nothing is fetched; locks are read without being created.
A local engine proved broken gets no download; model files cannot repair packages.

features.title: Pinned model identities and offline reuse
contracts: Every Kokoro, Chatterbox and Qwen3 model file has a pinned identity (repository, commit, size, SHA-256); a file of another size or content is damaged, never 'maybe newer'.
A verification record never vouches for bytes other than the pin: a changed file behind a valid record is hashed again and found damaged.
Only the pinned commit's folder is looked at, so a moved upstream main cannot change what is reported; a linked cache is unverified and never acquired over.
Files already verified are reused offline: a second install of an intact component downloads nothing and runs no pip.
A served file that is not the pinned one is never installed and leaves nothing to resume.

features.title: v3 authoritative planner and read-only workers (not wired)
contracts: The v3 planning worker's entry is disabled without an injected disposable context (exit code 2) and has no confirmation, installer or acquirer path.
Changed or forged v3 terms never spend a consent and fetch nothing; an all-ready plan is a no-op and planning spends nothing.
The read-only worker observes without filesystem writes, sockets or subprocesses and publishes only to its fixed exchange.

features.title: v3 sealed package and engine authority (not wired)
contracts: Packages can be consumed only under a held InstallLock and a live, spent operation; receipts, paths or plain objects grant nothing.
A rebuild never treats a missing or uncertain engine as approved damage.
The spaCy consumer is disposable-only: production v1 terms never grant it main-environment authority.

features.title: Voice sample and quality harness (developer)
contracts: An ordinary run writes one sample per registered voice (28), each through its own backend; one failing voice is reported and the others continue.
The final-acceptance judge reports each mechanical failure (incomplete decode, duration mismatch, implausible duration, clipping, pathological silence).
The QA corpus is original text whose identity hash changes whenever any item's wording changes.

features.title: Import Folder: one Book per folder of MP3s
contracts: A folder scan makes one Book per directory that directly contains MP3s; same-named directories never merge.
Import Folder replaces every Book; when any Book holds files or settings the user is asked first, and declining changes nothing.
A scan that finds no MP3s is reported in the log, not in a dialog.
Cancel Import stops a running scan and leaves the workspace as it was.

features.title: Add Files to the current Book
contracts: Chosen MP3s go into the current Book only, in the order the dialog returned them, whatever their folders.
A file already in the current Book is skipped and the Summary says how many were skipped.
Adding to a Book that already has tracks never changes its typed or cleared values.

features.title: Clear All Imports
contracts: Returns the tool to its startup state: one pristine Book, blank Shared values, no run result.
A pristine workspace is cleared without asking; any Book work or Shared value asks first, and declining changes nothing.
Source files and earlier outputs are never touched, and the log keeps its history with a divider.
Refused while a run or a scan is in progress (the button is locked).

features.title: Book navigation, add, duplicate and remove
contracts: Previous, Next and the selector move between Books by stable id, and each Book shows its own values.
Add Book adds a pristine Book; Duplicate Book copies settings but no tracks.
Removing a Book with files or edited settings asks first; a pristine Book goes without asking.
Book numbers are never reused while the workspace lives; a folder import or removing the last Book restarts at 1.
The selector label is 'Book N' plus the effective Album or source folder, elided after 40 characters.

features.title: Shared and per-Book metadata
contracts: Shared has exactly Artist / Author, Album Artist / Author, Album, Time and Book Artwork; a populated Shared value applies to every Book.
A populated Shared value disables the matching Book field without erasing the Book's own value, which returns when Shared is cleared.
The value written is Shared, else the Book's own, else blank; it is frozen into the plan when the run starts.

features.title: Pre-fill from source tags and Mixed source markers
contracts: A Book's first files pre-fill Artist, Album Artist and Album with the normalised majority of their tags (first seen wins a tie); a blank majority writes nothing.
Files added to a Book that already has tracks never change its stored values.
A field whose sources disagree shows 'Mixed source metadata' ('Mixed' in the tight layout); the marker is never a value.

Only a field with no value at all is filled by a Book's first files: a value typed or cleared before that import, a duplicate's carried values and the values an emptied Book kept all survive it, in the panel and in the tags written.

features.title: Intentional blank values
contracts: Clearing a field stores an empty value; the source value never comes back for it.
A blank Artist, Album Artist or Album is absent from the written tag, never inherited from the source file.
A blank Album leaves the combined file with no Title and no Album frame; nothing is invented.
A value cleared before a Book's first import stays cleared through it, in the panel and in the written tags.

features.title: Add or remove time at the end of each track
contracts: Blank or zero means no change; a positive number appends that many seconds of silence; a negative number trims that much from the end.
The adjustment applies to every track, including the last constituent of a Combine.
A trim that would leave less than 0.1 s fails that track before FFmpeg runs and publishes nothing for the Book.
Lengths are measured by fully decoding the audio, not from header claims.

features.title: Auto-number tracks and Start #
contracts: Auto-number is on by default per Book; Start # blank means 1.
With Auto-number on, each track gets TRCK as a plain integer and one zero-padded filename prefix, at least two digits and wider when the last number needs it.
With Auto-number off, there is no TRCK and no prefix.
Auto-number and Start # are per-Book only; they have no Shared counterpart.

features.title: Chapter Titles (track titles)
contracts: Until edited, the box shows each track's default Title: a usable source TIT2, else the cleaned filename.
Usable line n names track n; blank lines are ignored; a short list leaves the remaining defaults; extra lines are ignored.
The final Titles become TIT2, the filenames and the Combine timestamp labels.
The box locks while a run is in progress, like the other Book options and the Maker's and Editor's boxes; the panel still fills a locked box (v0.7.2, ACT72-014).

features.title: Track list reorder and remove
contracts: Move Up / Move Down move the selected tracks one step as a block, bounded at the ends; the selection follows.
Remove Selected drops only the selected tracks; the Book's settings stay.
Default Titles stay attached to their tracks through moves and removals.
Ctrl+A, Alt+Up / Alt+Down and Delete / BackSpace work on the list and obey the run lock.

features.title: Book Artwork (Shared and per Book)
contracts: JPG/JPEG and PNG are always offered; HEIC/HEIF only when the shared capability probe can decode it.
A chosen file is decoded first; a refusal shows an error and keeps the previous choice.
JPG/PNG are embedded as their own bytes; HEIC/HEIF become an in-memory PNG; the tag gets exactly one front-cover APIC, and no artwork means no APIC.
Shared artwork overrides every Book without erasing a Book's own choice.
Artwork that no longer decodes at run time fails the Book (not retryable) and publishes nothing.
Choose… and Clear each get at least their label's own width, so both read whole at every supported size.

features.title: Invalid Start # and Time are refused before a run
contracts: Start # must be a whole number of 1 or more (blank means 1); Time must be a finite decimal (blank means 0); NaN, infinity, units, commas and hex are refused.
Every Book is checked before anything is reserved; the first bad value shows an error naming the field and the Book, and no run folder is made.
The Book named in the error is its stable number, as the navigator and the run log show it, also after a removal (v0.7.2, ACT72-036; the Maker's Silence refusal likewise).

features.title: Run Write ID3 Tags or Combine for every Book
contracts: One press is one operation: it validates, reserves one run folder, freezes one plan for every non-empty Book and runs it on one worker with one controller.
Empty Books are skipped; with no Book holding tracks the user is told to import first and nothing is reserved.
A second operation is refused while one runs; workspace controls are locked for the run.
Edits made after the press never reach the run or its retry.
An unexpected worker fault settles the run as Failed, frees the panel and keeps the detail out of the Summary.

features.title: Write ID3 Tags output
contracts: Every track becomes a new clean copy in the Book's output folder; the source file is never written.
Each copy carries exactly TIT2, plus TPE1/TPE2/TALB when populated, TRCK when Auto-number is on and one APIC when artwork is set; every other source frame is gone.
Each copy is validated (present, non-empty, decoded length, exact frames and artwork) before the Book is published.
A Book is published only when every track passed; later Books still run.

features.title: Combine MP3s into one MP3 per Book
contracts: Each Book becomes exactly one combined MP3 in track order; Books are never joined with each other.
FAST concat is used when all constituents share codec, sample rate and channels; otherwise, or if FAST fails, Safe (WAV normalise then encode) is used and the reason is logged.
The combined tag is Title = Album, Album, Artist and Album Artist when populated, the artwork, and no track number or chapter frames.
combined_time-stamps.txt lists each final Title at its adjusted start offset with its length.
Concat lists quote paths with apostrophes, spaces and non-ASCII characters correctly.

features.title: Unreadable or damaged tracks
contracts: A file that does not fully decode fails with its own name and a retryable failure; its Book publishes nothing.
Other Books in the run still complete and publish.
A staged output that lost audio or carries the wrong frames is caught by validation and not published.
Embedded ID3/Info frames between joined MP3 segments are removed only in a private copy; real damage is never repaired.
Source files are byte-identical after the run.

features.title: Run folder reservation and output hint
contracts: Each operation reserves exactly one numbered run folder under <output base>/MP3-Tool-Outputs (MP3-Tool-N); building the panel creates nothing.
A failed run keeps its folder for Retry Failed, and a later run never reuses that number.
A run folder inside a source folder is refused.
The output hint shows where runs land, eliding from the left so the run folder stays visible.
If the run cannot be reserved or the plan is refused, the user sees the error and no empty run folder is left.

features.title: Output folder and file names, collisions
contracts: A Book folder is named from the effective Album, else the one folder that holds all its tracks, else 'Book N'; names are sanitised.
Repeated names within one run are numbered (Dune, Dune-1, Dune-2), including track filenames and a combined file that matches a track name.
Track filenames come from the final Title with one leading number removed and the calculated number added once.
No destination is ever a source file or inside a source folder, and publication never overwrites an existing file.

features.title: Private staging and whole-Book publication
contracts: Processing writes only to the run's private '.work' area; a Book becomes visible only when every planned output is staged.
Publication moves files into the Book folder and rolls back on any failure, so a Book is published whole or not at all.
A failed Book's good pieces stay in staging for Retry Failed; a published Book's intermediates are removed and an empty work area is deleted.
Cleanup never follows a link out of the work area.

Staging lives exactly as long as a Retry Failed can reach it: when a run settles, every Book it cannot retry loses its staging, and Clear All Imports, a new run and closing the tool remove the rest; a link planted in staging is unlinked as a link, never followed (v0.7.2, ACT72-019).

features.title: Cancel a run
contracts: Cancel stops a running FFmpeg or ffprobe step within a fraction of a second, through that step's own process handle, and otherwise stops the run at its next checkpoint (between tracks, stages or Books); no later FFmpeg step and no later Book starts.
Books never reached are 'Not attempted' and the batch ends Cancelled; a Book already published stays published.
Retry Failed is not offered after a cancelled run.

A stopped step is never a failed or retryable track and never the 999 launch failure; its half-written staged track or combined file is removed. Only that step's own process is stopped: any other FFmpeg, even one this program started, is untouched. Pause never stops or suspends a running step.
A cancelled run keeps no private staging: no Retry Failed is offered after a Cancel, so the run folder's .work goes before the run reports Cancelled (v0.7.2, ACT72-037).
A Book a Cancel stopped part-way reads 'Cancelled' and is counted as stopped by Cancel; Books the run never reached read 'Not attempted'. Both stay NOT_ATTEMPTED in the result (v0.7.2, ACT72-004).

features.title: Pause and resume a run
contracts: Pause asks the run to stop at its next checkpoint; 'Paused.' is shown only once the worker has stopped there.
While paused, Resume is offered and Pause is not; Resume continues the same run to its end.
An FFmpeg step already running is never suspended or stopped: it finishes, and 'Paused.' follows at the next checkpoint.

features.title: Retry Failed
contracts: Offered only when the run completed with failures and at least one failed track is retryable.
Re-runs only the failed tracks of the failed Books against the original frozen plan and run folder; later workspace edits never reach it.
Staged pieces that succeeded are reused, the Book is published whole, and Books that succeeded are not touched.
Item-less (Book-level) failures and cancelled runs are not retryable.

features.title: Book status and progress
contracts: The current Book shows Ready, Queued, Processing, Completed, Failed, Skipped or Not attempted, derived from the run, never stored.
One progress bar counts every track plus one finalisation step per Book; the status line reads 'Book X of Y — Track M of N'.
A batch with one failed Book among successes ends 'Completed with failures'.

features.title: Activity log history and Clear Log
contracts: Log history survives from run to run; a divider marks each run, each retry and each Clear All Imports, and import lines sit between.
Clear Log clears only the visible text; the event history, the session log and the run result are untouched and cleared lines never return.
Import problems go to the log, not a dialog; technical detail goes to Detailed and the session log, never the Summary.
Summary and Detailed follow new lines at the bottom and hold a reader who scrolled up (the shared view).

features.title: FFmpeg required
contracts: Only a proved, pinned FFmpeg/ffprobe pair counts as available; a merely discovered one does not.
Without it the panel shows 'WARNING: ffmpeg/ffprobe not found. Run the setup launcher to install it.'
A run without it fails each Book with an item-less, non-retryable failure and publishes nothing.

features.title: Panel layout, density and appearance
contracts: Four sections in order (1. Import & Books, 2. Book Settings, 3. Tracks & Run, Activity) with every required control fully on screen at 920x600 and larger, without a whole-panel scrollbar.
Below the measured floor the panel switches to the tight density; only the track list, Chapter Titles and log give up height.
Primary and job controls never overlap; Tab order follows the sections.
A live Light/Dark change recolours in place and keeps every Book, value, selection, log line and running job.

all_of.detail: Approve the captured MP3 Tool screenshots at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900 in Light and Dark.
Check the MP3 Tool at Windows display scaling other than 100%.

features.title: Closing the tool during work
contracts: Closing the window asks a running worker to cancel; it stops at its next checkpoint.
close() is idempotent, stops the scan poller and the pump, closes every component and leaves no scheduled Tk callback.
Destroying the panel always reaches close().
Alt+F4 during a long Combine exits with status 0, no window, no owned process and no Tcl crash.

features.title: Converter panel, layout and appearance
contracts: The panel shows 1. Sources, 2. Conversion & Metadata, 3. Output & Run and an Activity log, with Activity to the right whenever it fits.
The arrangement (wide, split or stacked) is chosen from the live widgets' measured sizes, never by a whole-panel scrollbar.
At 920x600, 1024x720, 1280x900 and 1920x1009 every required control is wholly on screen and the list and log keep their floor heights.
Switching Light/Dark recolors the panel in place without rebuilding it or losing imports, selection, options, log text or a running job.

all_of.detail: Approve the Converter screenshots captured at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900, and look at the panel once at a Windows display scale other than 100%.

features.title: Import M4B audiobooks
contracts: Only .m4b files are accepted, through Add Files and Add Folder alike; other extensions are refused by the shared validator, not just the dialog filter.
Add Files keeps the dialog's order; Add Folder recurses by default and keeps each file's root-relative provenance.
A very broad folder (a drive or the home folder) is confirmed before any scan starts; declining starts no worker and imports nothing.
The folder last chosen in either dialog is remembered for the next dialog.

features.title: FFmpeg readiness check
contracts: When the tool opens, the FFmpeg status line is written to both log panes; it never claims more than the shared status says (no bare 'FFmpeg detected').
Convert asks for a verified FFmpeg, not merely a found one; if it is not verified an 'FFmpeg is not ready' error is shown and no run starts.

features.title: Start a conversion: preflight and a frozen plan
contracts: Convert with an empty queue shows a 'No files' warning and starts nothing.
The queue and every option are read once on the main thread at Start; later edits to the list, options or fields cannot change the running run.
Every source is probed on the worker thread before any folder is reserved or any output written; progress is indeterminate until then and the denominator is the plan's segment count.
One failed book does not stop the others; the run settles SUCCEEDED, COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES, FAILED or CANCELLED.
Inputs and options lock while running and unlock when the run settles, even if the worker hits an unexpected error.

features.title: Whole book: one MP3 per audiobook
contracts: Whole book is the default output structure.
Each usable book produces exactly one MP3 covering the whole source [0, duration], named <source stem>.mp3.
A whole book is encoded in a single FFmpeg pass with no seek and no duration limit.
The produced MP3's audio matches the entire source.

features.title: Split by chapter: one MP3 per chapter
contracts: A chaptered book produces one MP3 per source chapter, in source order.
The outputs tile the whole source: audio before the first chapter belongs to output 1, gaps belong to the preceding chapter, and the last output ends at the source duration.
Each book's outputs go into their own folder named for the source file's stem, named 'NN - <chapter title>.mp3' with order restarting at 01 per book.
Each output's audio matches its exact source interval, first and last chapter included.

A split book that failed or was cancelled leaves no folder behind: once its finished segments are taken back, the empty folders made for it are removed with rmdir alone, never the run folder, never a folder holding anything, never through a link (v0.7.2, ACT72-029).

features.title: Books without chapters
contracts: A source that probes correctly and has no chapters is a success in both modes, never a failure.
In Split by chapter it becomes one whole-book file named <stem>.mp3 inside its book folder, with a log warning that it had no chapters.
That file is not a fragment: it gets whole-book tag rules, no structural track and no whole-run success number.
A probe that failed is never treated as chapterless.

features.title: Malformed chapter lists are refused
contracts: Chapter starts must be finite, not negative, before the source's end and strictly increasing; anything else makes the book unusable.
The check applies in both output structures and runs before any run folder is reserved; nothing is sorted, clamped, deduplicated or dropped to make a map pass.
A refused book is reported with its own reason and is not a Retry Failed candidate; the other books still convert.
The refusal says the chapter list is not usable and offers no other mode: both modes refuse it (v0.7.2, ACT72-026).

features.title: Unreadable or corrupt sources
contracts: A file FFprobe cannot read, a file with no audio stream and a file with no usable duration are each refused at preflight with their own reason.
A run in which nothing is usable converts nothing and creates no run folder.
Usable books in the same run still convert; refused books count as failures but are not Retry Failed candidates.
Sources are never modified.

features.title: Exact chapter boundaries (output-side seek, or the same samples from one decode)
contracts: On the seeking route a chapter's command places -ss after -i (output-side seek) and gives the span as -t (end - start), never -to.
Boundaries are chapter starts copied verbatim and written fixed-point to the microsecond; nothing is rounded.
Adjacent chapter outputs neither lose nor repeat audio, and the first output starts at source second 0.

On the continuous route (v0.7.2 Phase 7B, eligible books only) there is no seek: chapter k is exactly the decoded samples the output-side seek selects from the same -ss and -t strings, first half_up(S x rate) and count half_up(D x rate), cut at absolute positions and never by summing rounded durations, so every output is byte-identical to the seeking route's.

features.title: MP3 VBR quality
contracts: The chosen LAME VBR quality 0-9 (default 2) is passed as -q:a with libmp3lame for every output of the run, on every decode route.
The Converter never writes a constant bitrate (-b:a) and does not borrow the TTS bitrate contract.
A value outside 0-9 is clamped to 0-9 at Start and a non-number falls back to 2; the command builder refuses anything outside 0-9.

features.title: Metadata mode: Preserve, Replace, Write none
contracts: Preserve (default) carries only the source's title, artist, album artist, album and bare track number; a filled field overrides its own value.
Replace writes only the fields typed in; a blank field stays absent. Write none writes no tags, no chapter map and no cover (only FFmpeg's own encoder tag).
Every mode passes -map_metadata -1, so no other source tag (Audible IDs, MP4 brands, genre, comment) reaches an MP3.
Split outputs never carry the book's title: each gets its own chapter title and track. Every tagged output is ID3v2.3.
The four fields are disabled (never hidden) under Write none and while a run is going; typed text is kept.
The Title field is labelled 'Title', like its neighbours: blank keeps the source's title under Preserve and writes none under Replace; no filename is ever substituted (v0.7.2, ACT72-028).

features.title: Chapter markers and titles in whole-book MP3s
contracts: Whole book under Preserve or Replace keeps the source chapter map with unchanged timing and every chapter's title written back explicitly.
Write none keeps no chapter map and no titles; split outputs never carry a chapter map.
An output that keeps a chapter map is ID3v2.3 even when it has no text tags.
Non-ASCII chapter titles are read and written exactly (UTF-8 JSON from FFprobe, no code-page decoding); an untitled chapter stays untitled.

features.title: Embedded cover art
contracts: Exactly one stream marked attached_pic is the cover; an ordinary video stream is never artwork.
Preserve and Replace keep the cover on every output; Write none drops it. A book without a cover converts normally.
More than one embedded cover refuses the book at preflight in every mode; no cover is guessed.

Whole book: the cover rides in the single encode from a second opening of the same file, so long books are not truncated. Split: the cover is stream-copied onto each chapter in a second pass that leaves the audio bit-identical.

features.title: Auto-number tracks
contracts: Auto-number is off by default with Start # 1; it applies only to Whole book runs.
Each successfully written book takes the next track number from Start #; a failed, refused or cancelled book consumes nothing, so the sequence has no gaps.
A retry continues from Start # plus the number of books already written, not from Start #.
In Split by chapter, tracks are the chapter order restarting at 1 per book, whatever Start # says.

features.title: Run output folder and Open Output Folder
contracts: Each run writes into its own numbered folder under the output base's M4B-Converter-Outputs, reserved only after preflight finds at least one usable book.
An accepted run keeps the output base it started with even if Preferences change mid-run; the next run uses the new base.

The read-only Output field shows the destination hint before a run and the run folder after preflight; a finished or cancelled run asks the file manager to show its folder without waiting for it, after the run's closing line is written and the controls are released, so a busy or restarting Explorer never holds the window.
Open Output Folder reveals the last run folder, or the tool folder before any run, and shows an 'Output folder' error if that folder cannot be made.
A folder the file manager could not be asked to open is said in the Activity log with the reason and the folder's path; the run's result is not changed by it.

features.title: Output names, book folders and collisions
contracts: Whole outputs are <stem>.mp3; split outputs are 'NN - <title>.mp3', where slashes in a title become ' - ', a blank title becomes 'Chapter N', and the shared sanitiser handles reserved names, illegal characters and length.
Directly added files land flat in the run folder; a folder import mirrors its sub-folders; several roots get separate containers.
The whole run is one collision domain: same-named books or folders get -1, -2 suffixes and an existing file is never overwritten.
No planned destination can be one of the run's source files.

features.title: Codec compatibility: FFmpeg AAC and the Windows xHE-AAC decoder
contracts: Ordinary AAC books are decoded by FFmpeg; any decoder selection from the shared helper goes before -i. An ordinary book never takes the Windows route; a split AAC-LC book may be decoded by FFmpeg once (ACT.CONVERTER.SCALING), which leaves the Windows route and other codecs untouched.

An xHE-AAC book FFmpeg cannot decode completely is decoded by Windows Media Foundation when this machine can, once per book, with split chapters cut from the PCM at frozen boundaries and piped to the same encoder.
If no capable decoder exists the book is refused at preflight with no folder or output, and it is not retryable.
A decoder failure fails the output even when FFmpeg exits 0; a length mismatch names xHE-AAC as the cause only when the plan established it.

The PCM format the encoder is told is the format of the bytes the Windows decoder delivers: the reader decodes its first buffer before it answers, and a format the decoder changes after that is refused, never followed.

all_of.detail: Convert the owner's real xHE-AAC audiobook on Windows 11 in both output structures and confirm full length, chapters and cover.

features.title: Safe output writing: temporary file, length check, rollback
contracts: Each output is encoded into a temporary file beside its destination and moved onto its final name only after FFmpeg (and any cover pass) exit cleanly and the measured length is within 3% of the planned span.
A failed, cancelled or wrong-length output leaves nothing behind; an existing file at the planned name is never overwritten.
If one chapter of a split book fails, the book's chapters already written are removed; other books' outputs are untouched.
FFmpeg's diagnostics go to a temporary file, never an undrained pipe; only a bounded tail reaches Details. Sources are never modified.

features.title: Cancel a conversion
contracts: Cancel latches at once; a running FFmpeg is terminated (killed after a 5 s grace) and always reaped.
The interrupted output and that book's earlier chapters are removed; books already finished keep their outputs.
No further book is probed or converted; a cancel during preflight reserves no run folder.
The run reports CANCELLED only after cleanup; books never reached are 'not attempted', not failures.
The log says what Cancel does: the file being converted is stopped now and its book is taken back; books already finished are kept (v0.7.2, ACT72-027).
On the continuous route Cancel stops the encoder and the book's decoder and reaps both before the run settles (v0.7.2 Phase 7B).

features.title: Pause and Resume
contracts: Pause is a request: the status shows 'Pause requested.' until the worker reaches the next boundary (between sources in preflight, between outputs while converting).
The FFmpeg encode in progress is never suspended, frozen or killed by Pause; no new output starts while paused.
Resume continues the same run; Cancel wakes a paused run and ends it.
Pause is offered only while a run is going.

features.title: Retry Failed
contracts: Retry Failed is offered only after a run completed with failures that happened during conversion; preflight refusals are never retryable.
A retry re-runs only the failed books from the original frozen plan, at the original destinations in the original run folder, ignoring any later change to the list, options or Preferences.
The result is cumulative across attempts: earlier successes stay, a repeated failure replaces its record, an untouched failure keeps its own.
A retryable book with no plan entry is refused with a 'Retry Failed' error asking for a new run; nothing is re-probed or re-planned.
A retry of a book on the continuous route starts a fresh decoder and reproduces the clean run byte for byte (v0.7.2 Phase 7B).

features.title: Closing the Converter while it works
contracts: Closing sets the cancel latch and asks the controller to cancel (waking a paused run), so a running FFmpeg is terminated and reaped.
The worker is joined for up to 5 s; the job controls, importer and pump are closed and nothing stays scheduled.
destroy() always runs close() first; closing is idempotent.
The process exits cleanly with no window, no owned FFmpeg left running and no Tcl crash.

features.title: Activity transcript and Clear Log
contracts: The worker's per-file transcript and every FFmpeg command line go to Detailed only; Summary is the shared projection of the run's events.
A failure is named by book and output in Summary, with the exit code and a bounded FFmpeg tail in Detailed.
The FFmpeg status line on opening and the run's closing line appear in both panes.
Clear Log empties the visible Summary and Detailed text only; the run, its result and the session log are untouched, and the button never locks.
The run's closing line comes after the run's own Summary lines, and the run's end is said once (v0.7.2, ACT72-018: 'All done.' sat above 'Running.' and 'Finished.' came twice).

features.title: Long books and many chapters
contracts: A long split run produces every planned chapter, with spans that tile the whole book exactly however many chapters there are.
The Windows decoder route streams in bounded chunks and never stages the decoded audio to disk.
Progress counts outputs and the ETA comes from measured per-output times of the current attempt.

An eligible split book is decoded once by FFmpeg and its chapters are cut from that decode (v0.7.2 Phase 7B, ACT72-012): split mode, a chaptered book, FFmpeg's own decoder, one AAC-LC stream in fltp, a sample rate LAME takes as it is, mono or stereo with that layout, time base 1/rate, start 0, one AAC frame of priming or none, a packet timeline proven to be the running sample count with the declared total, a qualified FFmpeg build (by fingerprint), and an estimated saving, the prefix less PREFIX_PER_BOOK_SECOND times the duration, of at least the calibrated MIN_SAVED_PREFIX_SECONDS. The route is decided once at preflight and frozen into the plan; a retry keeps it with a fresh decoder.
Every other book, every whole-book output and every chapterless book keeps the seeking route, unchanged; anything that cannot be proven keeps it too.

The continuous route holds at most 1 MiB of audio, writes no decoded audio to disk, and changes only the audio pass: the encoder settings, the cover pass, the measurement and drift guard, staging and publication are the seeking route's, and every output is byte-identical to it.

A short feed, a stream ending part-way through a sample, a decoder that failed, was killed or produced other than the declared sample count fails the chapter, which takes its book back; nothing falls back to the seeking route part-way through a book.

features.title: Books workspace and navigator
contracts: The tool starts with one empty Book (Book 1 of 1) and keeps no file list outside the Books.
Previous, Next, the selector, Add Book, Duplicate Book and Remove Book are the shared workspace operations; Duplicate copies the settings but no tracks.
Removing a Book that has tracks or edited settings asks first; declining keeps it.
Each Book keeps its own tracks, fields and chapter text across navigation.
The selector shows 'Book N — hint', the hint being Title, else effective Album, else the one source folder.

features.title: Import Folder (one Book per folder)
contracts: Import Folder scans one chosen parent and replaces the workspace with one Book per directory that directly contains MP3s, tracks in natural order.
Separate directories are never flattened into one Book; an empty scan leaves one pristine Book.
Imported Books start with empty settings: no source tags are read to prefill fields.
If any Book already has tracks or settings, Import Folder asks before replacing; declining changes nothing.
A running scan shows its progress and Cancel Import; a very broad folder or a very large result asks first.

features.title: Add Files to the current Book
contracts: Add Files appends the chosen MP3s to the current Book only, never regrouping them by folder.
The chosen files are natural-ordered by name before being appended after the Book's existing tracks.
The Book's fields are untouched by adding files.
Files already in the current Book are skipped and the log says how many.

features.title: Track order and removal
contracts: Move Up and Move Down move the selected tracks one step as a block and stop at the edges.
Remove Selected removes only the selected tracks of the current Book; its fields are kept.
Alt+Up, Alt+Down, Delete, BackSpace and Ctrl+A act on the track list and are refused while a run locks the track controls.
Automatic chapter titles follow the new track order.

features.title: Chapter Titles box
contracts: Until edited, the box shows one automatic title per track: the filename with one leading track number removed and underscores cleaned.
Line n names chapter n; blank lines are skipped; fewer lines leave the remaining chapters automatic; extra lines are ignored.
The text is stored per Book and survives navigation.
The resolved titles are frozen at Build and are the M4B's chapter titles.

features.title: Shared and per-Book fields
contracts: Shared has exactly the Maker's six fields (Artist / Author, Album Artist / Author, Album, Series Name, Silence, Book Artwork); Title, Series Part, Output Filename and Chapter Titles are per Book only.
A populated Shared value disables the matching Book control and wins; the Book's own value is kept and returns when Shared is cleared.
Book values are stored raw; a cleared field is stored as blank, not deleted.
Effective values (Shared, else Book, else blank) are frozen into the plan at Build.

features.title: Silence Between Tracks
contracts: Blank Silence means 0; otherwise it must be a finite, non-negative number of seconds; negative, NaN, infinite or non-numeric text is refused.
Build refuses an unreadable Silence on any non-empty Book with a message naming that Book, before a run folder is reserved.
A positive Silence forces the Safe path and inserts one gap between adjacent tracks, never after the last.
The gap belongs to the end of the chapter before it; the next chapter starts exactly at its own track.

features.title: Series Name and Series Part numbering
contracts: Series Name (Shared or per Book) and a manual Series Part are written as the M4B's series tags; blank writes none.
Auto-number Series Part disables the manual Series Part entry (its value is kept) and numbers the Books that succeed consecutively from Start Part (blank means 1).
A Book that fails consumes no number; Retry Failed gives it the next unused number.
Start Part must be a positive whole number; otherwise Build stops with a message.

features.title: Book Artwork selection
contracts: Choose… offers only image types this machine can decode (JPG/PNG always, HEIC/HEIF only when decodable) and validates the chosen file before accepting it.
An undecodable or mislabelled image is refused with a message and the previous selection is kept.
