A Shared artwork overrides and disables the Book's artwork control; clearing Shared restores the Book's own.
The preview is an in-memory thumbnail; the chosen file is never written.
The control is disabled while a run owns it, separately from the Shared override.
Choose… and Clear each get at least their label's own width, so both read whole at every supported size.

features.title: Artwork embedded in the M4B
contracts: The effective artwork (Shared, else Book) is embedded as exactly one cover; JPG and PNG keep their exact bytes.
HEIC/HEIF is converted to PNG in memory at the same pixel size; no file is written beside the source.
Embedding rewrites metadata only; the encoded audio is unchanged.
An artwork that cannot be read fails its Book before any encoding and publishes nothing.

features.title: Output filename
contracts: The name is the first usable of: Output Filename, Title, effective Album, the one folder holding every track, 'Book N'.
The name is sanitised by the shared sanitiser and ends in .m4b exactly once; a name with no letter or digit left falls through to the next candidate.
Same-named Books in one run and existing files are numbered (-1, -2) deterministically; nothing is overwritten.
A path-like name cannot leave the destination, and an output can never be one of the inputs.

features.title: Standard run folder and output hint
contracts: Each Build reserves exactly one new run folder <output base>/M4B-Maker-Outputs/M4B-Maker-N and every Book of that Build lands directly in it.
A standard run folder inside a source folder is refused.
Staging lives in the run folder's private .work area, which no Book name can take, and is removed when empty.
The import band shows where the run lands, showing the end of the path behind an ellipsis when space is short.

features.title: Custom destination
contracts: 'Choose custom destination' is off on every new panel, reveals the path entry and Browse… only while on, and is never saved.
The folder is validated before anything starts; an invalid one shows a message and reserves nothing.
Outputs go directly into the chosen folder with no M4B-Maker-N inside it, numbered around existing files, never overwriting.
Staging happens outside the chosen folder, in an owned entry of the temporary work area that is removed once no retry can reach it (v0.7.2, ACT72-031).
While the toggle is off, a path left in the hidden entry is ignored.
A Cancel during a custom build leaves the chosen folder and every file it already held, including one named like a planned output; only Books finished before the Cancel are added (v0.7.2, ACT72-032).

features.title: Try FAST first (auto-fallback to Safe)
contracts: With Try FAST first on and no inserted silence, the FAST concat of the source MP3s is tried first.
A FAST failure falls back to Safe automatically and the Detailed log gives FFmpeg's reason.
With it off, Safe is used without trying FAST.
Both paths keep each chapter mark on its audible boundary.

features.title: Build M4B(s)
contracts: Build with no tracks in any Book warns 'Import a folder or add MP3 files first.' and starts nothing.
Build validates, reserves one destination, freezes one plan of every non-empty Book (empty Books are skipped) and runs it on one worker thread.
Edits made after Build (fields, tracks, artwork, options, destination) never reach the running or retried run.
Books are built in workspace order, each into one chaptered M4B with its tags and artwork.

features.title: Chapter timing and round trip
contracts: There is one chapter per track; each starts exactly at its track's first sample (no lead-in) and the last ends at the end of the audio.
FAST starts come from each source's fully decoded length, not its header estimate; Safe starts come from the WAV frame counts, silence included.
Splitting the M4B at its chapter marks gives back each source track whole.
264 chapters survive with their titles and ordered, non-overlapping timings.
Track paths containing an apostrophe build correctly.

features.title: Embedded tags
contracts: Title, Artist, Album Artist and Album are written from the plan's effective values.
A blank Title falls back to the resolved output name, so no Book is untitled.
ffmetadata syntax characters (=, ;, #, backslash) in tags and chapter titles come back exactly.

features.title: Staged build and atomic publication
contracts: FFmpeg writes only the Book's private staging file, never the final path.
The staged M4B is validated (audio present, planned chapter titles, Title and cover) before it is published.
Publication is an atomic move that refuses an existing destination; a work root on another drive goes through a temporary sibling.

A failed Book leaves no partial M4B under a final name and no staging, except a validated candidate kept for Retry Failed after a publication or numbering failure, and only while a Retry Failed can reach it: a cancelled, failed or abandoned run (Clear All Imports, a new Build, closing the tool) keeps nothing (v0.7.2, ACT72-031).
Source MP3s are never modified.

A custom-folder build stages in an entry of the owned temporary work area (kind 'maker'), listed with its owner before it exists; the entry is closed once no retry can reach it, and what a killed Maker left is recovered by a later custom build only once its owner is provably gone (never by name alone).

features.title: A Book that cannot be built fails alone
contracts: A track FFmpeg cannot read fails only its Book; the other Books still build and the run ends COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURES.
No M4B appears under a final name for the failed Book and its sources are unchanged.
The failure is one Summary line however many tracks the Book has, with FFmpeg's detail in Detailed.
A failure of the Book's inputs is retryable; unusable artwork or FFmpeg not being ready is a non-retryable failure of that Book.

features.title: Book status and run progress
contracts: The current Book's Status reads Ready, Queued, Processing, Completed, Failed, Skipped or Not attempted, taken from the run and never kept separately.
The status line under the progress bar names the Book being built as 'name.m4b (i of n)'.
When a run ends, Summary gets one line with completed, failed, skipped and not-attempted counts and the destination.
The worker thread never touches Tk; events from another run are rejected and never shown.
The run's result exists before its terminal event reaches the panel.

features.title: Cancel a build
contracts: Cancel is honoured at the next checkpoint: between Books and between steps inside a Book.
The Book being built publishes nothing and its staging is removed; Books not reached are Not attempted; Books already published are kept.
A cancel arriving while a Book is publishing keeps that Book and stops at the next boundary.

Cancel stops a running FFmpeg or ffprobe step within a fraction of a second, through that step's own process handle (any other FFmpeg is untouched), and no later step starts. A stopped step is never a failed encode: no FAST-to-Safe fallback and no retryable failure.
Cancel while a candidate kept from an earlier attempt is being checked or numbered discards it; no Series Part is committed and nothing is published.
A Book a Cancel stopped part-way reads 'Cancelled' and is counted as stopped by Cancel; Books the run never reached read 'Not attempted'. Both stay NOT_ATTEMPTED in the result (v0.7.2, ACT72-004).

features.title: Pause and Resume
contracts: Pause is acknowledged at the next checkpoint (between Books or steps) and nothing further runs while paused.
Resume continues the same attempt and the run then settles normally.
An FFmpeg step already running finishes; Pause never stops or suspends it.

features.title: Retry Failed
contracts: Retry Failed is offered only after a run settled with retryable failed Books, and is refused while a run is active.
It re-runs only those Books from the original frozen plan into the same run folder; edits made since Build are ignored.
Books that succeeded are not touched and the merged result describes the whole run.
A retained, validated candidate is reused, with a stale tentative Series Part rewritten to the next number.

features.title: Controls locked while a build works
contracts: While a run is active, Build, Import Folder, Clear All Imports, Add Files, Move/Remove, the navigator, Shared and Book fields, artwork, run options, the custom destination and the Chapter Titles box are disabled.
Track-list shortcuts are refused while the track controls are locked.
Everything is released when the run ends.

features.title: Clear All Imports
contracts: Clear All Imports returns the tool to its startup state: one empty Book, blank Shared, no run, Ready status and the default output hint.
It asks first only when there is meaningful work (a Book with tracks or settings, or any Shared value); declining changes nothing.
Nothing on disk is deleted or changed; the log keeps its history with a divider.
It is refused while a run or scan is active.

features.title: Activity history and Clear Log
contracts: Summary and Detailed keep earlier runs' lines; each attempt and each Clear All Imports adds a divider line.
Clear Log clears the visible text only and never interferes with a running build.

features.title: Panel layout, density and appearance
contracts: Four sections stack in order (1. Import & Books, 2. Book Settings, 3. Tracks, Chapters & Build, Activity) and nothing scrolls the whole tool.
At 920x600 and larger every required control is wholly on screen, with or without the custom path row.
Below the regular height the tight density reduces padding and shortens two option labels without hiding any control.
A Light/Dark switch recolours the panel in place without changing any Book, value, selection, option, log line or running build.

all_of.detail: Approve the Maker screenshots captured at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900 in Light and Dark.
Maker layout at Windows display scaling other than 100% (125%, 150%, 200%).

features.title: Closing the window during a build
contracts: Destroying the panel always reaches close(), which requests cancel of the run, closes the importer, stops the pump and closes every component; close() is idempotent.
Closing the application while a Maker build encodes exits with status 0, with no window, no owned process and no Tcl crash.
No partial M4B is left under a final name.
A closed panel stops listening for appearance changes.
Closing the tool lets the run go: a candidate kept for Retry Failed is removed at once, or by the worker as it ends if a build is still running (v0.7.2, ACT72-031).

features.title: Open the Metadata Editor panel
contracts: The launcher builds the panel through build_ui(parent), packed to fill its container
A new panel holds one pristine Book, blank Shared fields, status Ready and no run
Building the panel creates no output folder

features.title: Import Folder and Add Files (one file = one Book)
contracts: Import Folder scans the chosen folder and its subfolders and replaces every Book with one Book per .m4b/.m4a/.mp4 file, in order, even when several files share a folder
Add Files appends one Book per new file, skips a file already in the workspace and makes the last added Book current
Import Folder asks before replacing Books that hold a source or edits
Importing reads tags only and writes nothing

features.title: Import progress, Cancel Import and scan confirmations
contracts: While a folder scan runs the import status shows the count found and a Cancel Import button that stops the scan
A whole-drive or home-folder root asks 'Scan a very broad folder?' before scanning
A very large result asks 'Import a large number of files?'; declining imports nothing
A second import is ignored while a scan is active

features.title: Clear All Imports (workspace reset)
contracts: Clear All Imports returns the panel to one pristine Book with blank Shared fields, no observations and no run
A pristine workspace clears without asking; any source, edit or Shared value asks first, and No changes nothing
Nothing on disk is deleted or written; earlier outputs and the log history stay, with a divider marking the reset
It is disabled and refused while an action runs or a scan is active

features.title: Book navigation and Remove Book
contracts: Previous, Next and the selector move between Books; each Book keeps its own edits, chapter titles and artwork
Books are labelled 'Book N — <page title or filename>' and keep their number while the workspace lives
Remove Book on a page with a source or edits asks first; No keeps it; the file itself is never touched
There is no Add Book or Duplicate Book

features.title: Source read-back (what the file already carries)
contracts: Each source is read once, read-only, into a frozen observation: the seven text fields, series name and part with where they came from, cover presence and chapter titles
The Current Book shows the source name, folder and readability, a 'Detected on file' series line, and Series Part · Artwork · Chapters facts
An album-implied series name or track-implied part is shown as read-back only and never prefilled for writing
Read-back is display; it is never written to any file

features.title: Per-Book fields with preserve-by-default
contracts: Each Book shows its source's Title, Author / Artist, Album, Year, Genre, Comment and Series Name as prefill; showing them is not an edit
Only a keystroke stores an edit; a blank value or one equal to the source means keep the source's value
A changed value is written to that Book's copy only
A series value found in a vendor or movement tag is never moved to another tag unless the user changes it

features.title: Shared fields that override every Book
contracts: Shared fields start blank, even when every source carries the same value
A populated Shared value overrides that field for every Book and disables the matching Book entry
Clearing a Shared value restores each Book's own edit or source value
A blank Shared field writes nothing

features.title: Chapter Titles box (positional renames)
contracts: The box shows the source's chapter titles until the user edits it; showing them is not an edit
Line N renames chapter N; a blank or unchanged line keeps that title; blank lines are never collapsed; lines past the chapter count are ignored
Each Book has its own box
Renaming rebuilds only the chapter track with a stream copy; chapter count, boundaries, audio and cover are kept, and unchanged lines run no remux at all

FFmpeg exiting 0 after logging an error, or exiting non-zero, refuses the remux and leaves the copy untouched; the movie timescale stays pinned at 1000; freeform iTunes atoms the remux drops are restored

features.title: Shared and per-Book artwork (Choose… / Clear)
contracts: Choose… decodes the chosen image first; an unusable or undecodable file shows an 'Artwork:' error and changes nothing
A Shared artwork overrides and disables every Book's artwork control; clearing it restores the Book's own choice
Save Tags keeps the source cover unless a replacement is chosen; Clear All Tags removes it unless one is chosen; Remove Series Numbering never changes it
The chosen image file is never written
Choose… and Clear each get at least their label's own width, so both read whole at every supported size.

features.title: Auto-number Series Part and Start Part
contracts: Series Part is read-back only; it is never a Shared or Book text field
With Auto-number on, Save Tags and Clear All Tags give consecutive Series Parts from Start Part (blank = 1) to Books that succeed; a failed Book consumes no number
An invalid Start Part is refused with a 'Start Part:' message before any run folder is reserved
With Auto-number off, Save Tags keeps the source's Series Part; Remove Series Numbering never numbers

features.title: Starting an action: one reservation, one frozen plan
contracts: With no imported source an action shows 'Import a folder or add M4B files first.' and reserves nothing
Otherwise exactly one numbered run folder is reserved and one immutable plan is frozen; a planning error releases the empty folder and shows an error
Edits made after an action starts never reach that run
Each attempt runs on one worker thread that never touches Tk; events reach the panel through a queue
Planning itself creates no file and copies nothing

features.title: Save Tags and Clear All Tags (keep chapters)
contracts: Save Tags writes only the explicit edits (Shared over Book), a chosen cover and changed chapter titles onto copies; every other tag is the source's
Save Tags with nothing to change produces a byte-identical copy
Clear All Tags asks first, then writes copies with every tag and the cover removed and the chapters (markers and titles) kept
After the clear only the values typed here (Book edits, Shared values, chosen artwork, chapter renames) are re-applied; unchanged source values are not

features.title: Remove Series Numbering
contracts: After a confirmation, copies lose the Series Part, the track number and the movement index in every tagger namespace
The Series Name (on whichever tag carried it), chapters, cover and every other tag are kept
Pending Shared or Book edits, artwork and chapter renames are not applied, and Auto-number is ignored
The originals are never written

features.title: Declining a confirmation changes nothing
contracts: Answering No to Clear All Tags or Remove Series Numbering starts no run, reserves no folder and writes nothing
The workspace and its edits are left as they were

features.title: Unreadable source files
contracts: A file whose tags cannot be read is still a visible Book; its read-back says why and it prefills nothing
Actions skip it as 'Skipped (unreadable)' and the other Books proceed
When no imported file is readable the action refuses with 'None of the imported files could be read, so there is nothing to write.' and writes nothing
The unreadable file is never written

features.title: Copies into a numbered run folder (no in-place, no custom destination)
contracts: Every action writes copies into one new M4B-Metadata-N folder under the output base; originals are never opened for writing
Each copy keeps its source filename and extension, flat in the run; same names are numbered (Book.m4b, Book-1.m4b) and an existing file is never overwritten
A run folder inside a source folder is refused
There is no in-place save and no custom destination
The output hint shows where the next run lands, showing the tail of a long path

features.title: Open Output Folder
contracts: Before any run, opens this tool's output parent folder (creating it if needed); an output-path error shows a message
After an action has started, opens that run's folder

features.title: Audio, chapter and artwork preservation (no re-encode)
contracts: Audio is never re-encoded: tag edits rewrite atoms, the cover is a covr rewrite and chapter renames are a stream-copy remux
Unrelated tags are left exactly as they were

Before publication every copy is validated: readable audio, every planned write present, cleared fields absent, cover present exactly when the action leaves one, chapter titles in order, chapter count and boundaries unchanged, and a complete chapter track when it was rebuilt

features.title: Staged per-Book writes: a failed Book publishes nothing
contracts: Each Book is copied into its own staging folder under the run's .work area, edited and validated there, then moved into the run
A failure at any step (vanished source, unusable cover, copy, tags, cover, chapters, validation) publishes nothing for that Book and removes its staging folder
Publication never overwrites a file already at the destination
The .work area is removed once it is empty

A validated candidate kept for Retry Failed after a publication or Series Part failure stays only while a Retry Failed can reach it: a cancelled run keeps nothing, and Clear All Imports, a new action and closing the tool remove it (v0.7.2, ACT72-034).

features.title: Batch run order, per-Book results and status
contracts: Books run one at a time in workspace order under one controller per attempt
A failed Book does not stop later Books; the run ends 'completed with failures'
A Book that cannot start (for example unusable artwork) is a fatal, not-retryable failure; other failures are retryable for that file
Each Book's Status reads Ready, Queued, Processing, Completed, Failed, Skipped (unreadable) or Not attempted from the run's own records
The settled result exists before the finish event reaches the panel, and events from another run are ignored

features.title: Cancel a running action
contracts: Cancel stops a running chapter-title remux step (the ffmetadata dump or the chapter-track rebuild) within a fraction of a second, through that step's own process handle (any other FFmpeg, even one this program started, is untouched), and is otherwise honoured at the next checkpoint, between Books and between steps inside a Book; no later remux step starts
A cancelled Book publishes nothing and leaves no staging; Books already published stay; the rest are Not attempted
A Cancel arriving while a Book is being published keeps that Book and stops at the next boundary
Originals are never touched
A stopped remux is never a failed or retryable Book: no failure is reported and Retry Failed is not offered; its half-written .retitle.tmp output and its ffmetadata folder are removed
A Book a Cancel stopped part-way reads 'Cancelled' and is counted as stopped by Cancel; Books the run never reached read 'Not attempted'. Both stay NOT_ATTEMPTED in the result (v0.7.2, ACT72-004).

features.title: Pause and Resume
contracts: Pause is acknowledged at the next checkpoint (a Book boundary or between steps); nothing runs while paused
Resume continues with the next Book and the run finishes normally
A chapter-title remux already running finishes; Pause never stops or suspends it, and the run pauses at the checkpoint after it

features.title: Retry Failed
contracts: Retry Failed re-runs only the retryable failed Books of the same frozen run: same folder, same plan; edits made since are ignored
Books already published are not touched again
A validated candidate kept after a publication failure is reused, even if the source has since gone
Refused while an attempt runs or when nothing is retryable

features.title: Controls lock while an action runs
contracts: While an action runs, import buttons, Clear All Imports, the navigator, Shared and Book fields, artwork, the Chapter Titles box, the three actions and the series options are disabled
They unlock when the run ends
A second action while one runs is refused and reserves nothing
Clear Log and Open Output Folder are never locked

features.title: Activity log history and Clear Log
contracts: One Summary | Detailed log below the workflow; each attempt starts with a divider naming the action and run folder
History survives from run to run and through Clear All Imports
The Detailed pane lists each Book's steps ([artwork], [copy], [tags], [cover], [chapters], [validate]) in order; the Summary marks each published file
Clear Log clears the visible text only and is never locked

features.title: Layout, small-window density and keyboard order
contracts: Four sections (1. Import & Books, 2. Metadata, 3. Chapters & Save, Activity) stack in order and nothing scrolls the whole tool

At the launcher's 920x600 and 1024x720 content areas the tight density shrinks padding and shortens wording; no control is hidden, moved off screen or squeezed, and the preserve statement stays visible
Only the Chapter Titles box and the log give up height, down to their floors; choosing artwork does not grow the Metadata section
Tab moves through the sections in workflow order; Ctrl+A, Delete, BackSpace and Alt+Up/Down in a text field act on the text only

all_of.detail: Look at the panel at Windows display scaling other than 100% (for example 125% and 150%) at the launcher's smallest window

features.title: Light / Dark appearance
contracts: Every control uses the shared compact Light/Dark styles; the panel declares no colours of its own
A live Light/Dark toggle recolours the Chapter Titles box, the log panes and the selector list without rebuilding anything or changing any value or layout
Toggling during a run leaves the run, its locks and progress alone

all_of.detail: Owner approves how the Metadata Editor looks in Light and Dark

features.title: Closing the panel during work
contracts: Closing cancels a running action and any scan, stops the event pump and stops listening for appearance changes
destroy() always reaches close(), so a running worker is told to stop
Closing the app while a save runs exits cleanly with no window, owned process or Tcl crash left behind

features.title: Remembered dialog folders (and what is not saved)
contracts: The file and folder dialogs open in the last folder used (m4b_metadata.input_dir), the artwork dialog in the last image folder (m4b_metadata.cover_dir), or the home folder when that folder is gone
Only those two dialog locations are saved; the workspace, edits, Auto-number options and output folder are not

features.title: Open the Cover Image panel and its first-open defaults
contracts: Building the panel creates no output folder; the Output field names the tool folder, never a numbered run.
A fresh panel opens with Keep full image ticked, target size 1024, Save beside source images off with Create numbered copies preselected, the browser on Details and Include subfolders on.
The panel module imports and builds on a machine without HEIC support.

features.title: Import cover images (files, folders, type filters, Cancel Import)
contracts: Add Files keeps the order the dialog returned; Add Folder scans recursively and imports only the ticked image types, reporting other files as unsupported.
Move Up, Move Down, Remove and Clear All change only the imported list, never the files on disk.
A whole-drive or home-folder root asks before any scan thread starts; a result over the large-result threshold (1000 by default) asks before anything is committed.
Cancel Import stops only the scan and never reaches a running resize.

features.title: Duplicate images: refused by default, kept as separate occurrences when allowed
contracts: With Allow duplicate files off, adding a file already in the list adds nothing and reports it as a duplicate.
With it on, the same file becomes a second, independently selectable occurrence.
Two occurrences of one file stay two items through a run: two standard outputs, two numbered copies, two retry items.

features.title: HEIC / HEIF support follows the capability probe
contracts: HEIC/HEIF is offered for import, and in the file dialog filter, only when the machine can decode it.
A HEIC source is planned and written as HEIC; if this machine cannot encode HEIF the item fails with a clear message and no JPEG is written under any name.
A HEIC photo is not rotated twice (the decoder already applies its orientation).

features.title: Source browser views: Details, List, Medium Thumbnails
contracts: Details is the default view and shows Filename, Dimensions, Format, File size and Folder.
Switching between Details, List and Medium Thumbnails never changes the list order, the selection or the imported files.
Every view follows Remove, Clear All, Move Up/Down and new imports.
The view can still be switched while a resize runs.

features.title: Browser selection, keyboard and list shortcuts
contracts: Click, Ctrl/Command-click and Shift-click behave the same in all three views, and ranges follow list order.
Arrow keys, Home, End, Shift+arrows and Ctrl+A move and select without wrapping.
Delete/BackSpace remove the selection and Alt+Up/Down move it, through the same actions as the buttons.
Selection is refused while a resize runs, and the browser and the hidden shared list always agree.

features.title: Browser scrolling and lazy, bounded preview decoding
contracts: Only the visible rows or tiles are decoded, capped at 60 per request, off the main thread.
Previews live in one least-recently-used cache of 96 images; removed items release theirs.
Scrolling, including the mouse wheel over the thumbnail area, fills in rows and tiles that come into view.
Results that arrive after a removal, a newer list revision or close are dropped; closing joins decoder threads within a bounded wait.

features.title: Target size (square, px) and its validation
contracts: Every output is exactly size x size pixels for the size frozen when Resize Covers was pressed.

The size as typed must be a whole number of pixels from 256 to 4096 (the size box's own range); anything else (0, negative, a fraction, an exponent, nan, inf, a word) shows 'Bad size' and reserves and allocates nothing (v0.7.2, ACT72-025: a typed 0 became 1024 and 100000 reached Pillow).
Changing the size during a run does not affect that run.

features.title: Keep full image (letterbox into a square)
contracts: With the box ticked, the long side is scaled to the target size and the whole image is centred on a black square; nothing is cropped or stretched.
The box is ticked on a fresh panel and its value is frozen onto the run.

features.title: Center crop to a square
contracts: With the letterbox box unticked, the short side is scaled to the target size and the centre square is kept; the frame is filled with image, no bands.
The crop choice is frozen onto the run.

features.title: Output format follows the source format
contracts: JPG/JPEG sources are written as JPEG (quality 95) and PNG sources as PNG; the output keeps the source suffix.
Any other readable format is written as .jpg, and its destination is planned under that .jpg name.
JPEG and PNG output does not depend on HEIC support.

features.title: Phone photos come out upright
contracts: An EXIF Orientation tag is applied before resizing, and the output carries no rotating tag.
Thumbnails are upright, and Details reports the dimensions as the photo is seen (width and height swapped for quarter turns).
A photo without the tag is unchanged.

features.title: Standard output: a numbered run folder, planned before the run
contracts: A validated standard run reserves exactly one <output base>/Cover-Image-Outputs/Cover-Image-N folder and writes only inside it.
Individually added files land flat; one imported folder keeps its sub-folders; several imported folders each get their own collision-safe container.
Name clashes inside the run get -1, -2 suffixes, planned before the worker starts; a retry reuses the same destinations.
The Output field shows the tool folder before a run and the reserved run folder once it starts.
A destination plan refused after the run folder was reserved gives that empty folder back before the 'Output folder' message (v0.7.2, ACT72-061).

features.title: Save beside source images (mode switch)
contracts: The box is off on every fresh panel and Create numbered copies is preselected.
Create numbered copies and Replace original files are disabled until the box is ticked.
Unticking the box resets the choice to numbered copies, so a hidden Replace can never stay active.
Replacement is only reachable with the box ticked and Replace chosen; either alone gives a safe mode.

features.title: Create numbered copies beside the source
contracts: Each output is written beside its source as name-1.ext, never under the source's own name.
Existing numbered names are skipped (cover-1.jpg exists, so cover-2.jpg is written); numbering is kept separately per folder.
No standard run folder is reserved, and a planning failure leaves the source and its folder unchanged.

features.title: Replace original files safely
contracts: Every source is validated before the confirmation: a missing file, a folder, a link or a format written as .jpg (anything but JPG/JPEG/PNG/HEIC/HEIF) stops the whole run with 'Cannot replace originals'.
Each replacement is written to a temporary file beside the original, decoded and checked to be size x size, then installed with one atomic replace.
A failure before that install leaves the original byte-for-byte unchanged and removes only that temporary file.
Originals already replaced stay replaced after a later failure or Cancel, and the log says 'N of M original(s) replaced; any not reached are unchanged.'

features.title: Replacement confirmation dialog
contracts: Titled 'Confirm replacement of original images', it states the exact count, that the change is permanent and cannot be undone, and that completed replacements remain after a failure or cancel.

The destructive button reads 'Replace N Original Files' ('Replace 1 Original File'); Cancel is the default and holds focus, so Enter cancels; Enter presses whichever button holds the keyboard, so Replace only after the person has moved to it (v0.7.2, ACT72-060: Enter did nothing before).
Escape and closing the window cancel; declining creates no run, no temporary file and no output.
The dialog is built new for every run and every retry; there is no remembered answer.

features.title: Sources are never changed in the copy modes
contracts: In standard and numbered-copy modes no planned destination is ever an imported file, and every source is byte-identical after the run.
Two imports of one file in numbered mode never overwrite each other or the source.
Removing or clearing rows never deletes files, and reading Details or thumbnails never writes to an image.

features.title: Resize Covers: start a frozen run and lock the inputs
contracts: With an empty list Resize Covers shows 'No files' ('Please import images first.') and starts nothing.
The list, size, letterbox and mode are frozen when the run starts; later edits or imports cannot reach it.
Only one run at a time: pressing Resize Covers again during a run does nothing.
During a run the list, import options and resize options are disabled; everything unlocks when it ends.

features.title: Corrupt or unreadable images
contracts: A truncated or non-image file keeps its row, shows Unavailable for dimensions and format and a placeholder tile, and is never modified.
During a run it fails on its own, is named in the log, produces no output, and the other images are still published.
The run ends as completed with failures and offers Retry Failed.

features.title: Pause and Resume between images
contracts: Pause lets the current image finish and starts no new one; the run then reports Paused.
A paused run holds no half-written output.
Resume continues with the next image without redoing finished ones.

features.title: Cancel a resize run
contracts: Cancel stops the run after the current image ('Cancelling… will stop after the current image.') and also wakes a paused run.
Images not reached are reported as not attempted, not as failures; finished outputs and completed replacements stay.
The run is reported Cancelled only after the worker has acknowledged it.
Cancel never reaches an import scan, and Cancel Import never reaches the run.

features.title: Retry Failed
contracts: Retry Failed is offered only after a run with retryable failures.
A retry re-runs only the failed items with the original run's size, crop/letterbox choice and mode.
Standard-mode retries land at their originally planned paths and never overwrite an earlier success.

features.title: Progress, estimate and the run's Summary/Detailed report
contracts: Progress counts only images actually finished, also after Cancel.
Summary names each failed file without tracebacks or commands; Detailed keeps the technical error and the per-image transcript.
The estimate says calculating until three images have finished, and only successful images count.
Clear Log clears the visible Summary and Detailed text only.
The run's closing line comes after the run's own Summary lines, and the run's end is said once (v0.7.2, ACT72-018: 'All done.' sat above 'Running.' and 'Finished.' came twice).

features.title: Closing the panel or window during work
contracts: Closing asks a running or paused resize to stop, then waits a bounded time (5 s) for the worker.
After close nothing is scheduled on Tk, the import scan, browser decoders and run controls are shut down, and late events are ignored.
Closing the launcher window while Cover Image works exits cleanly with no crash.
A forced collection on a worker after close makes no Tk call and takes well under a second (about 23 s for TTS and 17 s for Cover before v0.7.2 Phase 6, ACT72-017).

features.title: Responsive panel layout (920x600 and up)
contracts: At 920x600, 1024x720 and larger windows every required control is wholly on screen with no whole-panel scrollbar.
Activity stays to the right of the workflow unless the panel is too narrow; the browser keeps at least one thumbnail row whenever Sources sits on top.
Only the browser views and the log scroll.

all_of.detail: Approve the Cover Image screenshots the launcher geometry journey captures at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900
Check the Cover Image panel at Windows display scaling of 125%, 150% and 200%

features.title: Light and Dark appearance in the Cover panel
contracts: Switching Light/Dark recolours the whole panel in place, including the thumbnail area, the hidden list and the log.
A switch keeps imports, selection, view, settings and log text, and rebuilds no widget.
Switching during a run leaves the run, its locks and its outputs untouched.

features.title: What Cover Image remembers, and what it deliberately does not
contracts: The folder last used by Add Files or Add Folder is saved as cover_resizer.input_dir and is where the next dialog opens; if it no longer exists the dialog opens at the home folder.
The saved key is accepted as user state without a settings warning.
Size, letterbox, Save beside source images and Replace original files are never saved; a rebuilt panel is back in standard mode.

features.title: Open each tool from the sidebar
contracts: The sidebar lists exactly six tools in registry order: TTS Audiobook, M4B Converter, MP3 Tool, M4B Maker, Cover Image, M4B Metadata.
Selecting a tool builds its panel once, shows it, marks its sidebar entry and sets the header title, description and the status line '<Tool> — ready.'
Every tool builds without an error panel on a healthy install.
On Windows the selected nav button keeps its enabled state (marked 'selected'), so it stays in the Tab order.

features.title: Switch tools while idle or while a job runs
contracts: Switching hides the current panel and never rebuilds or destroys it, so typed values, imported lists and a running job survive.
A job running in one tool keeps running, and finishes with complete output, while the user views another tool and comes back.
Switching tools, however often, creates no output folder.

features.title: Remember the last tool across launches
contracts: The selected tool is written to settings.json as last_tool on every selection and again on close.
On launch the saved tool opens if it is still available; an unknown or unavailable saved tool falls back to the first available tool without an error.
Tool choice and the Light/Dark choice set by real clicks survive a close and relaunch.
Window size and position are deliberately not saved (ACT.LAUNCHER.WINDOW-SIZE).

features.title: Window opens at 1024x720 and stays usable down to 920x600
contracts: On Windows the launcher opens at 1024x720 every time and cannot be made smaller than 920x600 (macOS opens at and is limited to 1024x800).
Every tool's core controls stay wholly on screen from 920x600 to maximized, in Light and Dark, with no core scrolling.
Window size and position are not carried over to the next launch.
The process is not DPI-aware, so at 125% or 150% Windows scales the same 96-DPI layout.

all_of.detail: Windows display scaling other than 100% (125%, 150%) is not exercised; HOME-PC runs at 96 DPI.
Approve the screenshot candidates captured at 920x600, 1024x720 and 1400x900; no visual baseline is approved yet.

features.title: A tool that fails to load shows an error panel
contracts: A tool whose module raises while loading shows a read-only error text inside its own panel; the launcher keeps running and the other tools load normally.
An invalid voice registry is reported as entries to correct in scripts/tts/voice_registry.py, never as a missing dependency.
Any other load failure advises running the setup launcher again and includes the technical details.
The status line never calls a tool that failed to load 'ready': it says '<Tool> failed to load.' each time that tool is selected (v0.7.2, ACT72-041).

features.title: Open log folder
contracts: 'Open log folder' creates files/runtime-data/logs if it is missing and opens it in Explorer without a console window.
A failure to open the folder never raises into the window.
On Windows the action is a real button reachable by Tab, Enter and Space.

Showing a folder never waits for the file manager, in any tool: the shared request is made on one background thread, one folder at a time; a folder already waiting is not asked for twice, at most four wait, and the thread is never joined, so closing the application does not wait for Explorer either.

features.title: Start-up sequence and one-time start-up reports
contracts: Configuration warnings, the last cleanup's result and the start-up notice are each presented once, after the window exists; any error while presenting them is logged and the launch continues.
A start-up notice handed over by the launch appears once in the status bar, never as a dialog, and is removed from the environment.
Fatal-fault diagnostics are armed and pydub is pointed at the proven FFmpeg before any tool panel is built.
The HuggingFace model cache is redirected into files/runtime-data/models/huggingface before any engine import.
Starting the app creates no output folder.

features.title: Private staging and atomic publication for M4B Maker and Metadata Editor
contracts: A staging directory must sit directly under the operation's work root and the staged file directly inside it, or nothing is touched.

Publication refuses an unstaged file, an existing destination or a link, and moves atomically (via a temporary sibling when the work root is on another drive), so the final name never holds a partial file.
Discard removes only the staging directory's own entries; symlinks and junctions are removed as links and never followed.
The work root is removed only when empty, and never through a link.

features.title: Close the app while a tool is working
contracts: Closing the window (Alt+F4 or the title-bar close) while any tool works ends the process with status 0, leaves no window and no child process the app started, and does not crash Tcl.
After the main loop ends the launcher ends only the ffmpeg.exe/ffprobe.exe processes it started itself; others are left alone.
Every tool panel reaches its own close when its window is destroyed.
Closing during a folder import cancels and joins the scan and adds nothing.
The launcher holds its Tk root for the life of the process, so a closed root is never freed on a worker thread.

Once the main loop has ended the launcher finishes the closed window's Tk variables, images and fonts on the main thread, so a collection that lands on a worker afterwards makes no Tk call and waits for nothing (v0.7.2, ACT72-017; the forced-landing arms check both).

features.title: Cooperative cancellation primitive
contracts: raise_if_cancelled does nothing for a missing or false check and raises ConversionCancelled ('Cancelled.' by default) for a true one.
is_cancelled answers a real bool under the same rule, without raising.
A worker written against raise_if_cancelled works unchanged with a JobController's cancel_check.
Import cancellation never reaches a processing job: the import coordinator does not use this module.

features.title: Pause, Resume, Cancel and Retry Failed controls and the run state machine
contracts: Buttons are enabled only where the state allows: Running offers Pause and Cancel; Pause requested and Paused offer Resume and Cancel; idle, cancel-requested and ended runs offer none; Retry Failed only after 'completed with failures' with a retryable failure.
Pause and Cancel are requests: 'Pause requested' is shown until the worker reaches a checkpoint; Cancel outranks Pause and wakes a paused worker.
A run settles exactly once; Cancel and a result being made final race under one lock and exactly one wins.
Retry Failed re-runs only the retryable failures of the exact original frozen run.
Workers never touch Tk: events cross a queue and are drawn on the main thread; a call from another thread is refused before any widget is touched.

features.title: Locked inputs, disabled controls and keyboard reach during a run
contracts: While a run is Running, Pause requested, Paused or Cancel requested, the imported list, its buttons and shortcuts and every registered processing option are disabled; they re-enable when the run ends.
Job controls, log tabs, progress/status and Open Output are never locked by a run.
A locked list ignores Add, Move, Remove, Clear and every keyboard shortcut.
Tab reaches every visible core control of every tool, in workflow order, at 920x600 and 1024x720, and never stops on a hidden one.
Audited across the six tools in v0.7.2 Phase 6 (ACT72-014): every option a run freezes is registered; the TTS Resume, Edge rate and Kokoro speed and the MP3 Chapter Titles box were not, and now are.

features.title: Progress bar, stage line and time remaining
contracts: The bar shows exactly the projected progress as 'done/total  N%': an unknown total animates instead, and an unfinished, cancelled or failed run keeps the count it reached and is never rounded up to 100%.
Progress never goes backwards within one scope.
The stage line names the stage and current item; the time remaining reads 'Calculating…' until there is enough evidence, and while paused or after the run ends.
Retiring the view stops an animating bar's timer.

features.title: Summary and Details log panes
contracts: Two read-only tabs: Summary (progress, warnings, failures and the output location; never technical detail) and Details (every accepted event, timestamped, including technical detail).
Earlier runs and the panel's own lines stay above the live run; a re-render replaces only the live section; clearing empties the visible text and the same run does not refill it.
Ctrl+A selects all text in either pane, and copying works although the panes are read-only.
Each pane keeps at least one readable line however small the window.

Each pane follows on its own: while its newest line is on screen (a tolerance under one line) new lines keep it at the bottom; scrolled up, the reader keeps the same top line to the pixel through new lines, trimmed history, a rewritten live section, resizes and tab or tool switches, and follows again on returning to the bottom.

A render changes only the lines that changed (an append, the lines trimmed off the front, or the rewritten tail), never the whole pane, and every render and view change runs on the thread that owns Tk.
An appearance change re-colours both panes in place and keeps a following pane at the bottom.
A run that ended says so once: when the stream holds the run's own ending event, the controller's change into that terminal state adds no Summary line (v0.7.2, ACT72-018).

features.title: Session log files and crash diagnostics
contracts: Each launch writes one timestamped session_<date>_<time>.log under files/runtime-data/logs.
Only the newest logging.max_sessions logs are kept (default 30); if configuration cannot be read the default applies and logging still starts.
A native crash dumps every thread's Python stack into this session's own log; failing to arm that never stops the app.
Technical job events reach the session log exactly once, and a rejected event is never logged.

features.title: Add Files and Add Folder importing
contracts: Add Files keeps the order the dialog returned; Add Folder scans in the background and adds files depth first in natural order (1, 2, 10), roots in the order chosen.
Only ticked supported types are imported; hidden folders are skipped unless 'Include hidden folders' is ticked; 'Include subfolders' (on by default) controls recursion.
A file already in the list is skipped and reported unless 'Allow duplicate files' is ticked.

A broad root (a drive or share root, or the home folder) is confirmed before any scan starts, and a result over the configured threshold (default 1000) before anything is added; declining adds nothing.
An import appends in one step or not at all: a failed, cancelled or declined import leaves the list exactly as it was, and a second import while one is scanning is refused.

features.title: Cancel Import
contracts: While a folder scan runs the status reads 'Scanning… N files found' (a live count, never an estimate) and Cancel Import is enabled; otherwise it is disabled and reads 'No import running.'
Cancel Import stops the scan, shows 'Cancelling the import…' and adds nothing even if files were already found.
Cancel Import never touches a processing job, and a job's Cancel never touches an import.

features.title: Imported file list: order, selection, remove and Clear All
contracts: Rows read '<n>. <relative path or file name>' under a count line '<N> files imported — <M> selected'.

Extended selection (Shift-click, Ctrl-click, Ctrl+A); a selected block moves as one with Move Up/Move Down or Alt+Up/Alt+Down and keeps its internal order; each button is enabled only when its action can apply.
Remove, Delete, BackSpace and Clear All remove rows only; no source file is touched.
Selection follows the occurrence, not the row index, so a moved row stays selected and two deliberate duplicates are two independent rows.
Shortcuts are bound to the list itself, so they never fire while typing in a field.

features.title: Confirmation questions: No changes nothing
contracts: Broad or destructive actions ask a Yes/No question on the main thread before anything is committed (broad-root scan, large result, Clear All or Remove Book with work in it, clearing or renumbering tags, Reset Preferences).
Answering No changes nothing and starts nothing.
A pristine Book is cleared or removed without asking; a Book holding any imported file, configuration value or Shared value asks first.

features.title: Books: navigate, add, duplicate and remove
contracts: The navigator shows 'Book X of Y' with ◀ Previous, Next ▶, a Book selector, and the Book actions the tool offers (Add Book, Duplicate Book, Remove Book; the Metadata Editor offers Remove Book only).
Previous is unavailable at the first Book and Next at the last; navigation does not wrap.
Add Book appends a pristine Book and selects it; Duplicate Book copies every configuration value, starts with no files, is inserted right after its source and is selected.
Remove Book selects the Book that took its place; removing the only Book leaves one pristine Book.
A folder import makes one Book per folder that directly contains files, in first-appearance order, with files in natural order.

features.title: Shared Metadata overrides per-Book fields
contracts: A populated Shared field applies to every Book and disables the matching per-Book field.
A blank Shared field leaves each Book's own value in force; clearing a Shared field restores the Book's untouched value and re-enables its field.
A value of only spaces counts as blank; stored values are never stripped.
Fields resolve independently, and each tool declares its own field list.

features.title: Per-Book runs, outcomes and Retry Failed
contracts: Starting a run freezes every eligible Book into its own run snapshot; later edits to the workspace, including Shared values, cannot reach the run.
Empty Books are skipped as 'skipped empty' and invalid Books as 'skipped invalid'; neither stops the batch from succeeding.
Each Book ends as succeeded, failed, skipped empty, skipped invalid or not attempted; a Book cancelled part-way through its own work is failed.
Retry Failed re-runs only failed Books that hold a retryable failure, against the frozen run; skipped and not-attempted Books are never retried.

features.title: Gap-free series numbers for successful Books
contracts: With auto-numbering on, numbers start at the chosen start value and only a Book that actually succeeded uses one, so a failed middle Book leaves no gap.
Asking for the next number uses nothing; confirming the same proposal twice is an error, never a silently skipped number.
The start value comes from the frozen run, not the live workspace.

features.title: Output folders, run folders and safe file names
contracts: Each run writes into <output base>/<Tool>-Outputs/<Tool>-N, where the base defaults to ~/Downloads/Audiobook-Creation-Tool-Outputs and N is the lowest free number, claimed atomically when a validated run starts.
Starting the app, building or switching panels and opening or saving Preferences create nothing; an empty, unused run folder is released.
A name that already exists or is already planned in the batch gets the next '-N' variant (case-insensitively); names are cleaned of Windows-forbidden characters and reserved names.
A destination equal to an input, inside a source tree, or reached through a link or junction is refused.
Each panel's read-only output-folder line follows a saved or reset output base without rebuilding the panel.

features.title: Safe replacement through a temporary sibling
contracts: A replacement is first written to a uniquely named temporary file beside the original (same folder, same disk) and then swapped in with one atomic replace.
atomic_replace refuses any source that is not one of its own temporary files, and discard_temporary refuses a real file.
A write, validation or replace failure leaves the original unchanged and no temporary file behind.
A linked, missing or folder source is refused for replacement.
Numbered copies beside the source never reuse the unnumbered name and never collide with each other.

features.title: Saved settings file and malformed-file recovery
contracts: User state is stored only in files/runtime-data/settings.json; config.toml is never written.
Writes are atomic (temporary file, then replace) and report success; a failed write leaves the previous file intact and rolls the in-memory value back.
A missing file means defaults; malformed JSON or a non-object falls back to defaults with a recorded reason, and the file is not rewritten on load.
Only keys the app itself writes are recognised; an unknown key is reported and can never override configuration.

The module's own description names exactly what is saved (the last tool, input and cover folders, the custom output location, Light/Dark) and that window size and run options are not (v0.7.2, ACT72-043).

features.title: Configuration defaults, config.toml and the launch warning
contracts: The effective configuration is the code defaults, then each valid key from config.toml, then the one allowed settings override (the output folder).
Each key is checked on its own: a missing or malformed config.toml, a bad value or an unreadable settings file falls back without stopping the app, and one bad key never discards a good one.

Problems are shown once per launch in one non-modal 'Configuration warnings' window with a plain summary and Continue (Escape also closes it); technical detail goes to the session log; reloading or opening Preferences does not repeat it.

The archive is downloaded only after the person says yes; declining exits 2, downloads nothing and changes nothing

features.title: Environment health assessment on every launch
contracts: An interpreter that does not run, has no ssl, runs on another copy's Python, or has package files missing under intact metadata is repairable (exit 3 to the launcher)
An out-of-range Python or broken Tk is repairable only when a better base Python exists; otherwise the environment launches degraded (exit 0)
No display is reported as degraded, never as a broken environment, so it cannot trigger a rebuild loop
A healthy assessment costs one subprocess and never installs anything

features.title: Automatic environment rebuild (repair route)
contracts: A repair runs from a base interpreter (never the venv's own) and rebuilds only the Python environment and its packages; it never runs full setup and never installs FFmpeg itself
The old .venv is renamed aside and put back if the new one fails to build, install, import or launch
A voice engine held under .venv/engines is carried to the new environment at the same path and never deleted
An interrupted repair is finished first on the next start before anything else touches the environment
After a repair the launch never asks for a second repair; a still-running environment whose repair failed opens with a notice

What setup says about FFmpeg is what it does: the environment rebuild never touches FFmpeg, and the launch that follows a repair run checks it and repairs it like every launch; the --repair-venv help and repair_venv's docstring say exactly that.

features.title: Preferences: Repair App Environment
contracts: The button asks for confirmation first; declining changes nothing
Confirming writes one repair-request file inside .venv and removes nothing; the running app and any conversion in it are left alone
The next start reads the request as 'repair-requested' and rebuilds through the ordinary repair route, keeping the Qwen3 engine

features.title: Hash-locked pinned dependencies and the verified package store
contracts: Where the lock describes the interpreter (Windows x86-64 CPython 3.12) every package comes from the lock, each checked against its SHA-256, and installs never reach an index
A package the lock does not name cannot be installed, and a kept file whose hash is not the locked one is refused
Only the lock's exact verified artifacts stay in files/runtime-data/python-packages; anything else is quarantined, never installed
A complete store reinstalls with no download; pip is never upgraded and runs with its cache inside the app folder and no inherited pip configuration
The committed lock is a faithful, complete freeze of scripts/requirements.txt

features.title: Requirements stamp, import proof and launch-time package reconcile
contracts: A success stamp is written only when pip succeeded and every required import was proved; either failure writes nothing, so the next start retries
A changed requirements.txt or lock is reconciled once, in place, at launch; the environment is never deleted or recreated for it and no model is downloaded
A package missing despite matching pins is detected by a presence probe and repaired
A real import proof is re-established after 7 days or when the interpreter changes

features.title: FFmpeg pair proof and health record
contracts: A pair is ffmpeg and ffprobe from one directory, and it is usable only after both halves actually run (bounded, hidden -version calls)
The proven pair is pinned in a local state file and reused while both binaries are unchanged; a changed or deleted binary invalidates the pin
While the pin holds, a launch executes no other candidate on the computer
Another copy of the app's files/bin is never this copy's pin
The failure text says retrying the same launcher will not help and never suggests turning protection off

features.title: The app's own pinned FFmpeg build (Windows)
contracts: Only the one pinned download URL is used, and the archive's SHA-256 is checked before anything is extracted
Every archive member is vetted first (no absolute paths, traversal, links or absurd sizes)
The pair is proved in staging, promoted with one directory rename into files/bin/ffmpeg/<version>, proved again there and only then pinned
Any failure before the pin leaves the previously working pair active

features.title: FFmpeg repair at setup and on every launch
contracts: First-run setup and every normal launch use the one repair_ffmpeg orchestration, so a launch with a missing or broken FFmpeg repairs it rather than only warning
Windows never runs a package manager: the route is the pinned pair on file, then the app's own verified build
Ready means the health record holds a proved pin; an installer's exit code never decides it
A launch whose repair fails still opens the app in limited mode with one notice naming only the routes actually tried
An FFmpeg problem never rebuilds the Python environment, and a second launch after a successful repair does no work

features.title: Launch-time Kokoro check and package self-heal; Chatterbox probe
contracts: The Kokoro proof imports the synthesis chain offline and builds no model; it never downloads weights or spaCy's model
A broken Kokoro install gets one in-environment repair through the one package installer; a repair whose proof still fails is recorded and not rerun the same day
A proof that cannot finish is 'unverified': no repair, an honest notice, nothing recorded as healthy
Missing Kokoro weights are reported, not downloaded, and are not a failure; an Application Control block is explained in plain words
The Chatterbox health probe runs in a subprocess against the venv, downloads no weights and builds no model

features.title: Optional voices: read-only plan, review, one-click consent, contained install
contracts: Choosing components is not consent: a read-only plan is made first and shown in full; nothing is downloaded before the person presses Install Selected Components
The click mints exactly one consent whose terms are exactly what the worker derives from the shown plan; a second click does nothing and Install is never the Enter-key default
Skip, Cancel and closing never download anything and keep what already works; Try again makes a new plan and needs a new confirmation
The setup worker runs only in the app's .venv and only if its whole process tree can be contained; a timed-out worker and its children are ended
Each request gets exactly one terminal result, published once and never replaced
The install log follows new steps while its reader is at the bottom and keeps a reader who scrolled up (wheel or scrollbar) in place

features.title: English sentence data for the Edge voices (NLTK punkt_tab)
contracts: The data comes from one pinned commit; the archive and every installed file are checked against pinned SHA-256s and installed with one rename
Anything that does not match (hash, unsafe member, not a zip) installs nothing
NLTK reads only files/runtime-data/nltk_data, never the user's profile
First-run setup discloses the download before Begin Setup and a failed fetch is not fatal; when the data is missing an Edge conversion asks first, and No starts nothing and downloads nothing
The 'sentence data missing' message names the Start button.

features.title: Offline restore of Kokoro's spaCy English model after a rebuild
contracts: After every proved reconcile, a missing spaCy English model is reinstalled offline from the kept wheel, with no index, no dependencies and its hash enforced
Nothing runs unless the kept wheel is a plain file of exactly the approved size and SHA-256
The restore runs only after every required import was proved; an unproved reconcile restores nothing
A failed reinstall is logged and never fails setup or repair

features.title: Install-folder depth check and eSpeak NG short data path
contracts: Setup and repair refuse an app folder too deep for Windows before anything is installed, with one clear instruction; the limit depends on whether Windows long-path support is on and no Windows setting is changed
When the bundled espeak-ng-data path is too long for eSpeak NG's buffer it is linked (never copied) under a short project-owned root that fits
An installation that already fits is left completely alone, and when no short root can be used the failure stays truthful

features.title: Engine lease: environment changes never race a Qwen3 install, conversion or worker
contracts: Before setup recovery or an environment repair changes .venv, all three Qwen3 locks (setup, inference, engine) are taken in one order, or none
A busy lock is an immediate refusal that changes nothing and says what is running
The lease is held through the whole replacement, including a rollback, and released in reverse order even when the work raises
A holder that dies releases its locks; another copy's machine-wide GPU guard does not block this copy

features.title: Preferences: Clear Downloaded Data (review, confirm, post-exit cleanup, result)
contracts: The review lists exactly four items (Private Python environment, Portable binaries, Downloaded voice models, Application logs) with state, size and consequence; nothing is preselected

After the app exits the helper removes exactly the selected items (.venv itself; the other three emptied) and writes one result
The next launch shows that result exactly once

features.title: Clear Downloaded Data target safety (closed catalog, links, protected paths, engines)

A target swapped for a link is refused; a link inside a target is removed as a link and never followed
A .venv holding a separately installed voice engine is refused and not offered; items a Qwen3 user can reach are removed only under the engine lease
Nothing is removed if the requesting app does not exit in time, and the request is consumed before the first deletion so it can never run twice
The helper never runs on a virtual environment or on any interpreter inside the app folder except the app's own base Python, which no cleanup target contains

features.title: Release packaging allowlist

Developer-only entry points, the verification gate, development trees, environments, caches and runtime data never ship
The packaged and committed config.toml ship [development] developer_mode = false, checked again in the finished archive
A build refuses uncommitted changes and occupied destinations, validates every member against its source and publishes all or nothing
The ordinary build produces only the Windows archive

features.title: Application version identity
contracts: scripts/shared/version.py holds the single application version string

A config.toml project.version that disagrees is warned about and the code version wins

After a successful launch a detached helper closes the Terminal window without the 'terminate running processes' prompt

features.title: Optional-setup v3 read-only planning supervision (production-disconnected)

Cancel before start never executes anything
A non-main interpreter is refused before native qualification

Metadata admission has fixed ceilings (16 MiB canonical plan, exact limits) that a caller cannot supply, using the standard library only

issues.resolution: Fixed in v0.7.2 Phase 6 (6E): epub2tts_edge._run_ffmpeg runs both M4B steps through Phase 6C's subprocess_utils.run_supervised (hidden window, stdin the null device, output to temporary files) and still raises CalledProcessError on a non-zero exit. Each step has a deadline, m4b_step_deadline: the parts' playing time read from their headers plus ten minutes (run_supervised's new deadline_seconds, opt-in, None for every other caller; at the deadline the child is stopped and reaped and subprocess.TimeoutExpired is raised). Measured on HOME-PC with the production arguments, the concat runs at about 2,600 times and the AAC encode at about 380 times the playing rate. make_m4b runs both steps inside _ctrl_c_stops_the_step: on the main thread a Ctrl+C is recorded, the supervisor stops that very child through its own handle (terminate, then kill), no further step starts, and the press is raised as KeyboardInterrupt on the way out; main() prints one line and exits 130 for Ctrl+C, 124 for a deadline. Reproduced at 5a87ec3 with the real command line in a console of its own and a step slowed to the playing rate: Ctrl+C waited 28.6 s for FFmpeg to finish (traceback, STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT); a suspended FFmpeg hung it for good. After: exit 130 0.16-0.17 s after the press, the step's FFmpeg gone by process id and creation time, no later step, nothing published, the output folder (a same-named file with --overwrite included) and the sources byte-identical, the work folder removed, nothing of the run left in its job, an FFmpeg sentinel of the same process alive; a step ignoring terminate with repeated presses killed after the 2 s grace; a suspended FFmpeg stopped at its deadline, exit 124. Evidence files/dev-work/verification-gate/outputs/2026-11-09_phase6e_work_1fbd/act72-010/ (test_edge_cli_m4b_interrupt.py).

issues.title: M4B Converter split cost is O(chapters x duration): every chapter decodes the source prefix (output-side -ss, deliberate)
issues.evidence: files/dev-work/verification-gate/outputs/2026-11-04_233658_phase0_2b7d/issues.json
issues.resolution: Fixed in v0.7.2 Phase 7 (7A measured and designed it; 7B implemented and qualified it). Reproduced at c4a9b6a: each chapter decoded all audio before it again, 1.3-1.6 s per hour of prefix. scripts/m4b/m4b_continuous.py decodes an eligible split book once with FFmpeg to pcm_f32le and cuts each chapter at absolute sample positions from the same -ss/-t strings the seeking route writes (m4b_commands.segment_times), encoded through pcm_argv/run_argv_streaming with the cover pass, measurement, drift guard and publication unchanged; every output is byte-identical. The route is decided at preflight and frozen in the plan: AAC-LC fltp, a LAME rate, mono or stereo, time base 1/rate, start 0, priming 0 or one frame, a packet scan proving the timestamps, a qualified FFmpeg build (fingerprint), and an estimated saving P - 2.0 x D of at least 600 s (calibrated before qualification); anything unproven keeps the seeking route. Qualified on HOME-PC at 90fcb3d (application code identical to the candidate 6a92e03), gyan.dev FFmpeg 9.0.1 full_build, Python 3.12.10: verify.py --mode qualification --scenario m4b-scaling PASS, 79 of 79 checks over 207 runs (2026-11-10_124457_qualification_c208). T1 6 h/48 chapters 2.16x wall, 2.28x CPU; T1b 1,000 chapters 2.88x wall, 3.76x CPU; the 12 h book 1.58x (reported); T2 unchanged below the threshold and 0.79-0.93 of the seeking time above it; T3 slope at most 0.002 s per hour of prefix; T4 at most 610,968 bytes of audio held, no PCM on disk; T5 staged bytes no higher; T6 heartbeat p99 0.015 s, no stall over 2 s; T7 Cancel settled in 0.25-0.75 s with every process reaped; T8 every output of every run equal to the pinned reference; encoder and decoder kills taken back and retried identically with a fresh decoder. Attempt 1 at 6a92e03 failed on three harness defects (the Converter's end-of-run Explorer reveal left live, a mistimed encoder kill, pipe bytes counted as disk writes), corrected in 90fcb3d with budgets and threshold unchanged. Record: files/plans/ACT-v0.7.2-Phase7A-M4B-Converter-Baseline-and-Design.md section 13.

issues.title: The Converter's real Media Foundation decode (xHE-AAC and other codecs FFmpeg cannot decode) is exercised by no automated test; every m4b_winaudio test drives a fake reader
issues.evidence: v0.7.2 Phase 4 inventory review (read from source, not measured)
issues.resolution: Closed in v0.7.2 Phase 8. Routine: files/tests/test_m4b_winaudio_real.py runs the production reader (IMFSourceReader, no stand-in) on real generated books in three stream shapes, held to the container's coded-frame count and to FFmpeg's own decode of the same file, and runs the Converter's whole Windows route (plan, reader, pipe, encoder, publication) on a real book in both structures. Recorded qualification on HOME-PC (Windows 11, 2026-11-10, ignored evidence): the owner's real xHE-AAC book (sha256 b9a24a88...f8d4, 35,199.625 s, 15 chapters), read only, decoded whole by the production reader at 44.1 kHz stereo to 35,199.7794 s (100.0004 %), and converted by the real panel, routed by its own plan, as a whole book (35,199.779 s) and by chapter (15 files, 35,199.627 s in all, worst chapter 0.0007 s from its span), every file decoding clean. Not qualified: any other xHE-AAC book, Windows 10, a Windows without the media feature pack. Listening remains the owner's check (xhe-aac-real-book).

issues.title: The gate's picture of a window could include the owner's taskbar and a black band, or be refused, depending on where Windows had placed the window: a journey enlarged the window where it stood, so at 1400x900 on a 1920x1080 desktop it ran under the taskbar, and only 25 points of the picture's rectangle were tested for anything lying over it
issues.evidence: v0.7.2 Phase 8 final full gate on 052bef1 (2026-11-10_175132_full_3527): launcher.six-tools-at-three-sizes BLOCKED, 'another window covers the owned window at 166,1043'; the window at that point was Shell_TrayWnd (0,1032)-(1920,1080). The same refusal in 2026-11-10_083655_changed_26e7. With the window placed lower the bottom row of points fell below the screen and the picture was kept: tts-1400x900.png and the other five 1400x900 pictures of 2026-11-09_170309_full_7178 (the Phase 7B full gate) and of 2026-11-10_123220_changed_422d show the taskbar and a black band, and hide the window's last 107 rows
issues.resolution: Fixed in v0.7.2 Phase 8: native_input.resize_client moves a window that would reach past its monitor's work area back inside it and refuses a size the work area cannot hold; native_input.screenshot tests the rectangle every four pixels and along its far edges and refuses a point on no monitor; resize_and_check records that the whole client area is inside the work area at each size. control.partly-hidden-window-is-not-pictured places a strip that all 25 former points miss and then hangs the window off the desktop, and passes only when both pictures are refused. No check was removed or relaxed. The pictures kept by earlier runs are unchanged evidence of those runs; the six 1400x900 candidates from them are not fit to be baselines and the candidate list of the final gate replaces them.
